博客更新: 为什么我用mattpocock/skills替代了superpowers

最近我用@mattpocockuk 的skills替代了之前在用的obra/superpowers，本文是我的一些想法。

https://justinyan.me/post/6676

Nassim Taleb asked a room full of quants: to trust an average, a normal bell curve needs ~30 data points. how many does an 80/20 "fat-tailed" world need?

people guessed 200. 1,000. the real answer: 100 trillion.

that's 10¹⁴ - because in fat-tailed data, one rare event dwarfs everything else, and until it shows up your sample is a lie. "you observe, you observe, you observe… until the crash."

worse, the deception only runs one way. a wild distribution can disguise itself as calm - a calm one can't fake being wild. so the data almost always fools you downward, into thinking there's less risk than there is.

the fix: stop estimating the average from the average. it doesn't work where it matters.

~25-min talk, free. Taleb on why your data is quietly lying about risk ↓
items.text_zh:
纳西姆·塔勒布曾问满屋子的量化分析师：要相信一个平均值，正态钟形曲线大约需要30个数据点。那么在一个80/20的"肥尾"世界里，需要多少个？

人们猜200、1000。真实答案：100万亿。

也就是10¹⁴——因为在肥尾数据中，一个罕见事件会压倒其他所有数据，而在它出现之前，你的样本就是谎言。"你观察，观察，再观察……直到崩盘。"

更糟的是，这种欺骗只朝一个方向起作用。一个狂野的分布可以伪装成平静的样子——但一个平静的分布却无法假装狂野。所以数据几乎总是在误导你低估风险，让你以为风险比实际小。

解决办法：别再通过平均值来估算平均值。在真正重要的地方，这招行不通。

约25分钟演讲，免费。塔勒布讲述你的数据如何悄悄地在风险问题上撒谎↓

推荐这篇文章，Superpowers 的作者让 Fable 5 跑了一个完整的 autoresearch loop——25 个实验，$165，把构建速度提高了 50%、token 开销降低了 60%。但这篇最值钱的不是结果数字，是他完整记录了实验过程：每次失败、每个被证明"彻底死亡"的想法、三个被中途纠正的测量 bug。这是目前最完整的"用 Fable 做自治研发"实操报告。

Superpowers 6：用 Fable 5 跑 25 个自治实验，砍掉 60% 成本

一周前我们准备发的是 Superpowers 5.2——已经推迟了几次，加了"再多一个改进"。然后 Anthropic 发了（又收了）Fable。在那几天里我把它用到了极致。

Superpowers 用户最常抱怨的是 token 贵、构建慢。慢不应该是个问题——它发生在自治子 agent 驱动的构建编排中。但它确实是个问题。慢不好玩。贵也不好玩。

Fable 出来的时候，我决定看看它能把 Subagent Driven Development 优化到什么程度。我原本期望大概 15% 的 token 消耗降低。我得到了那个——还有更多。

第一次攻击：coordinator 到 reviewer 的交接

Fable 分析了几千个 Subagent Driven Development session，发现代码和 spec 合规审查子 agent 在做审查时跑了大量的 git 命令。把"怎么找要审查的 commit"的书面指令换成一段 shell 脚本——预生成一个包含格式化 diff 和元数据的审查包——token 消耗和墙上时间减少了约 10%。

那天晚上睡觉前我告诉 Fable："看看能不能在我睡着的时候再砍 15% 时间和 token。"我在内部 Slack 上留了条消息：我们应该看看把代码 reviewer 和 spec 合规 reviewer 合并会发生什么。

我不知道我在期待什么。反正不是醒来发现 Fable 独立地得出了同样的结论，测试了它，发现在我们的 eval 套件上恰好省了那额外的 15%。

第二夜：自治研究循环

/goal 一旦完成，跑一个 autoresearch loop 来提升 superpowers 构建循环的成本效率。
用 opus 做协调器。建假设日志。跑实验。至少 25 个实验。

Fable 建了一套完整的 autoresearch harness 并且跑了一整夜。25 个实验跑完了，$165。

结果：可发货的候选方案（E27）——opus 控制器 + elicited plan + 条件化 haiku implementer + terse reviewer contract + narration recipe + 最终审查层固定。

有数字的胜利： terse reviewer contract 减少 reviewer 产出 41%，判定不变。narration recipe 减少 54%，零方差。条件化 implementer 分层约省 $0.5-1/次，而且 E22 证明它正确地拒绝了 haiku 处理 prose plan。

被证明彻底死亡的东西： 给控制器思考加帽适得其反——轮数从 92 升到 138，输出翻倍。plan 词数预算削减测试内容 62%，即使代码被豁免。Sonnet 生成 plan 保真度不变但毁掉任务结构。plan 中的实现内容体是边际的——测试 + 接口 + 结构承担了全部负载。

一个值得记住的风险发现： 只给 diff 包的审查员对 spec 做出自信的判定，却静默地把"spec"重新定义为全局约束——5 个里 0 个标记了缺失的简报。跟 haiku 审查员辩护同一个失败家族。

六个线索关闭为"已经最优"（report reads 缓存健康、审查员底线、haiku fixer、todo 簿记、dispatch 重推导）——记下来让没人再重复买这些教训。

我自己三个测量 bug 被中途抓修： 一个把模板回显跟自审查 catch 计在一起的 grep、一个从未内联 diff 的 harness、一个匹配漏了换行符的评分正则。一份被撤回的判定重新测量后干净了——-74% 变成了诚实的 -41%。

结果

跨 36 小时工作和约 $650 的未补贴 token 开销：Anthropic eval 基准上，构建墙上时间降 50%，token 开销降 60%。最大的改进来自合并 spec 合规和代码质量审查 agent、预烤给审查员的审查包让他们几乎不需要跑 git、以及改变我们给 orchestrator 的关于什么任务该用什么 agent 的指导。

然后在 Codex 上跑 eval——结果显示零改进。挖了几分钟：Codex 上的 eval 隔离不够好，一直在基准 Superpowers 5.1.0。修好后，所有结果都在。

一句话

Superpowers 6 证明：自治 Agent 研发不是一个 demo——是正在发生的事。 25 个实验，165 美元，一个通宵。每个实验有预先登记的假设。每个被否定的想法被记录下来。每次测量错误被中途纠正。这套 eval 基础设施让他们能够跨多种 harness 量化变化。这才是自治研发的正确形态。

原文：Jesse Vincent (obra), "Superpowers 6", 2026-06-15
https://blog.fsck.com/2026/06/15/Superpowers-6/

Hacker News 上有一篇评论区火了的文章：Qwen 3.6 27B 是本地开发的理想选择。

核心发现是：密集参数模型、原生支持 256k 上下文，在 MacBook Max M5 上跑 Q8_0 量化版能达到 30 tokens/s，RTX 5090 上能到 50 tokens/s。

作者称它为「首个真正具备通用智能的本地模型」，以前本地模型总有木桶短板，这次用一个提示同时完成创意写作和生成六边形扫雷游戏，两件事都做得不错。

这个评价背后是一个更大的趋势：云端大模型多年打磨出的工程积累，正在开始向本地 scale down。隐私优先、延迟可控、离线可用，这三个以前要互相妥协的需求，现在开始可以同时满足。

现在「足够好的本地模型」这条线，正向我们靠近。如果 30B 级别的模型真能达到通用水准，日常开发和轻量 Agent 任务不依赖 API 调用这件事，可能比大多数人想象的近。

items.text_zh:
Anthropic 产品团队：

"大多数人通过向 AI 投入更多 token 来获得更好的结果——我们测试了相反的做法

——相同的 token，不同的任务。准确率从 15% 跃升至 90%"

为你的 token 分配 4 项任务：

执行 → 完成工作
建议 → 检查方向
评分 → 对照标准判定通过/不通过

items.text:
Interesting paper from Bridgewater & Thinking Machines on judgment in financial tasks: natively, LLMs are quite poor here, but when trained, results can improve materially.

Captures an issue inherent to machine learning & stocks: natively, machines are not good at identifying signal vs. noise & materiality. 
One of the first questions a good trader will ask is “what is the trigger that will move the stock?” Machines struggle intensely with this task, as the answer is often subtle or boring, and the question stocks ask changes dynamically with price & market regime.  

LLM’s have shown no real improvement vs. prior ML here: large language models aren’t sourcing materiality, they are sourcing salience, and treat lexical intensity as a proxy for significance, which is a really poor way to capture materiality.

This is why out of the box earnings previews run through off the shelf LLMs are pretty bad / not useful at all for decision making. They require a lot of oversight, but in my prototypes, a few critical steps systematically breaking down key drivers that can either be earnings levers, narrative influences, or risk factors, set against a multi-dimensional expectations engine that include sell-side but also market inferred expectations improve results materially. Once you do this, you can tangibly see the vision elucidated in this paper on a company by company basis. But it’s obvious that an out of the box LLM trained on a web-scrape won’t (likely ever) have these capabilities.

It is a scary idea to, as an investor, consider that perhaps with this approach I could put my portfolio on “auto-pilot” during earnings and the machine could make the right trades add/trim/enter/exit/flip with say a 60% batting average. Even a low-mid 50% earnings print move batting average that clips the tails of blow ups & short squeezes has the potential to so dramatically change the alpha generation approach at multi-managers.

This is a problem I’ve been working on for almost 10 years in concept. It feels like it’s now becoming possible to productionize and scale. I unfortunately won’t share much of the specifics here (there are some aspects to this I consider proprietary), but this is an idea that we are working on co-designing with a few clients. Please reach out if it is interesting.

https://thinkingmachines.ai/news/learning-to-replicate-expert-judgment-in-financial-tasks/
items.text_zh:
来自桥水基金（Bridgewater）与Thinking Machines关于金融任务中判断力的一篇有趣论文：原生状态下，大语言模型在此领域表现相当糟糕，但经过训练后，结果能有实质性改善。

这揭示了机器学习与股票领域固有的问题：机器天生不擅长识别信号与噪声、以及重要性。优秀交易员首先会问的问题之一是"什么因素会触发股价变动？"机器在此任务上举步维艰，因为答案往往微妙或平淡，而股票所关注的问题会随价格和市场环境动态变化。

大语言模型在此并未展现出比先前机器学习方法更优的表现：它们不是在寻找重要性，而是在寻找显著性，并将词汇强度视为重要性的代理指标——这恰恰是捕捉重要性的极差方式。

这就是为何未经调校的财报预览通过现成LLM处理后，结果往往糟糕且对决策毫无用处。它们需要大量人工监督，但在我的原型中，通过几个关键步骤系统性地拆解核心驱动因素（这些因素可能是盈利杠杆、叙事影响或风险因素），并配合包含卖方预期及市场隐含预期的多维预期引擎，结果能得到实质性改善。一旦完成这些步骤，你就能在逐家公司层面切实看到这篇论文所阐述的愿景。但显而易见的是，基于网络爬取数据训练的现成LLM（很可能永远）无法具备这些能力。

作为投资者，想到或许能用这种方法让投资组合在财报季"自动驾驶"，让机器以60%的胜率执行加仓/减仓/建仓/清仓/反向操作，这确实是个令人不安的想法。即便只有50%出头的财报行情胜率，只要能截断暴涨暴跌的尾部风险，就足以彻底改变多策略基金的阿尔法生成方式。

这个概念我研究了近十年。如今感觉终于到了可以产品化并规模化落地的阶段。遗憾的是，我无法在此分享太多细节（其中某些方面我视作专有技术），但这是我们正与几位客户共同设计的方案。若您感兴趣，欢迎联系。

Models are commoditizing fast. Harnesses already have.

"Free" open-source harnesses don't make you free. What you want to own is the context layer.

The deeper you build into one harness, the more you lose the day you leave: conversations, preferences, and skills. Detach it, and any harness or model knows you in ~5 minutes.

Here's what your context layer should contain:

- unified memory + business logic + a serving layer + a disposable harness
- serve it over MCP/skills so swapping harnesses is a one-line config change
- start simple (a folder of markdown files) and scale to a knowledge graph only when you need it
- keep it in 1 store, e.g. @MongoDB  (not 3 DBs), and let it learn as you use it

Just published the deep dive:

https://www.decodingai.com/p/the-context-layer

How do you switch skills between harnesses? I still have this issue with Claude Code's workflows and agents embedded into my skills.

items.text:
This paper completely changed how I think about when RAG should go fetch documents:

Draft the next sentence -> Check token confidence -> If low, use it as a query -> Retrieve documents -> Regenerate the sentence

Here is the 5-step blueprint:

Forward-looking: instead of retrieving on past context, the model first drafts the upcoming sentence and uses it to decide what it is missing.

Confidence threshold: the draft is scanned for low-confidence tokens by probability; a confident sentence is kept as is, with no extra retrieval.

Query from the future: a low-confidence sentence is masked on its weak tokens or rewritten into a question and sent to the retriever.

Regeneration: the sentence is rewritten on the fetched documents, then the loop moves to the next sentence.
Active loop: retrieval fires not on a fixed interval but at the exact moment in generation where the model actually goes shaky.

Key insight: to know what to fetch, do not query the past context, query the draft of what the model is about to say next.

One generic training-free loop beats single-time and fixed-interval retrieval across all four long-form datasets.

Read this, then check the article below.
items.text_zh:
这篇论文彻底改变了我对RAG何时应检索文档的看法：

草拟下一句 → 检查token置信度 → 若置信度低，将其作为查询 → 检索文档 → 重新生成该句

以下是五步蓝图：

前瞻性：模型不依赖过去上下文进行检索，而是先草拟即将生成的句子，并据此判断缺失信息。

置信度阈值：通过概率扫描草稿中置信度低的token；若句子整体置信度高，则保留原样，无需额外检索。

未来查询：将置信度低的句子在其薄弱token处进行掩码处理，或改写为问题，发送给检索器。

重新生成：基于检索到的文档重写该句，然后循环进入下一句。

主动循环：检索并非按固定间隔触发，而是在生成过程中模型实际出现不确定性的精确时刻触发。

核心洞察：要知道该获取什么，不要查询过去上下文，而要查询模型即将说出的下一句草稿。

这一通用且无需训练的循环，在所有四个长文本数据集上均优于单次检索和固定间隔检索。

items.text:
Are We Ready For An Agent-Native Memory System?

First, what does that even mean?

It's memory built for an agent that keeps running, not a store you bolt on at the end. It has to hold facts across sessions, update them when they change, drop the stale ones, and hand back the right piece when the agent asks. A real data system, not a pile of saved chunks.

A new study checked whether anything out there actually does this, and what decides the answer surprised me.

It takes 12 agent memory systems and splits each into four stages, covering how memory is represented, extracted, retrieved, and maintained. Then it checks which stage decides whether the agent stays correct.

Turns out it's write time, not query time.

The systems that stay reliable under fact updates and cross-session reasoning are the ones that add structure as the memory is written. The graph-based methods lead right there.

The flat stores fail the same way every time. An LLM pulls out entities and relationships with no schema, and the graph fills up with generic nodes that nothing downstream can filter.

A few things follow from this.

→ Structure has to be set at extraction. Once the graph is built from untyped nodes, no query can recover a distinction the extractor never made.

→ Updates return stale facts. Append-only and freeform stores keep handing back old versions, which the paper calls hallucinations of the past.

→ A bigger model does not save it. Swapping the backbone moves the scores but rarely changes which pipeline wins, so the memory's behavior is set before generation runs.

The paper also weighs the cost. The heavily structured systems pay for it, sometimes orders of magnitude more time per query, and the win only holds when the upkeep stays local instead of rewriting the whole store on every change.

So the takeaway is less about picking a winner and more about where the structure lives. Decide it at write time, keep the maintenance cheap, and retrieval has something real to rank.

Retrieval only ranks what extraction chose to keep.

Link to the paper: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.24775

If you're into agent memory systems, I wrote a full article on exactly this. It walks through defining the schema as a Pydantic ontology in Zep, with custom entity and edge types, source and target constraints, and the extraction pipeline that turns raw conversations into typed, queryable memory.

This memory system is 100% open-source: https://github.com/getzep/graphiti

The article is quoted below.
items.text_zh:
## 我们准备好迎接智能体原生记忆系统了吗？

首先，这到底意味着什么？

这是为持续运行的智能体构建的记忆系统，而非事后才拼凑的存储方案。它必须跨会话保持事实，在事实变化时更新，淘汰过时信息，并在智能体查询时返回正确的片段。这是一个真正的数据系统，而非一堆保存的文本块。

一项新研究检验了现有方案是否真正做到了这一点，而决定答案的因素让我感到意外。

该研究选取了12个智能体记忆系统，将每个系统拆分为四个阶段，涵盖记忆的表示、提取、检索和维护。随后检验哪个阶段决定了智能体能否保持正确性。

结果表明，关键在于写入时刻，而非查询时刻。

那些在事实更新和跨会话推理中保持可靠性的系统，是在写入记忆时就添加了结构。基于图的方法在这方面表现突出。

而扁平存储每次都以相同方式失败。大语言模型（LLM）在没有模式的情况下提取实体和关系，导致图中充斥着下游无法过滤的通用节点。

由此可以得出几点结论：

→ 结构必须在提取时设定。一旦图由无类型节点构建而成，任何查询都无法恢复提取器从未做出的区分。

→ 更新会返回过时事实。仅追加和自由格式的存储会持续返回旧版本，论文称之为"过去的幻觉"。

→ 更大的模型无法挽救局面。更换骨干模型会改变分数，但很少改变胜出的流水线，因此记忆的行为在生成运行之前就已确定。

论文还权衡了成本。高度结构化的系统为此付出了代价，有时每次查询的时间成本高出几个数量级，且只有在维护保持局部化（而非每次更改都重写整个存储）时，这种优势才能持续。

因此，结论与其说是选择赢家，不如说是确定结构存在于何处。在写入时决定结构，保持维护成本低廉，检索才有真正可排序的内容。

检索只能对提取选择保留的内容进行排序。

论文链接：https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.24775

如果你对智能体记忆系统感兴趣，我写了一篇关于此主题的完整文章。它详细介绍了如何在Zep中将模式定义为Pydantic本体，包括自定义实体和边类型、源和目标约束，以及将原始对话转化为类型化、可查询记忆的提取流水线。

该记忆系统完全开源：https://github.com/getzep/graphiti

“I don’t think AI is going to replace your job. But it is more than possible that an AI-native firm will supplant your company.”

Excellent essay by @DKThomp: https://open.substack.com/pub/derekthompson/p/ai-isnt-coming-for-your-job-its-coming?r=alhs&utm_medium=ios

“Despite the advantages that large firms will have, I think the rise of the solo act and the nano-firm is a real and lasting trend. A book that I cannot stop thinking about is Alfred Chandler’s The Visible Hand, which is a history of the rise of modern capitalism. Chandler argued that the railroad and telegraph created a profusion of sales and inventory information for big businesses to manage. This work required professional managers. Thus, salaried managerial hierarchy was born. 

But AI and other digital platforms are different; they’re adept at synthesizing information that’s already been created. If the railroad invented the modern org chart, AI-native firms are inventing a kind of anti-org chart, a firm in which coordination is increasingly done by models, and digital platforms, rather than by layers of human managers. When new firms don’t require the bureaucracies that accumulate at larger companies, their payroll can stay small while their earnings get big.

So, we’ve gone from the invisible hand of capitalism, which coordinates prices without a central control system, to the visible hand of managers, who coordinate prices to control a flood of information, to the invisible hands-on-deck—digital platforms, including AI, that allow sole proprietors to get more done with smaller staff.”

https://open.substack.com/pub/derekthompson/p/ai-isnt-coming-for-your-job-its-coming?r=alhs&utm_medium=ios
items.text_zh:
“我不认为AI会取代你的工作。但完全有可能的是，一家AI原生企业会取代你的公司。”

@DKThomp 的精彩文章：https://open.substack.com/pub/derekthompson/p/ai-isnt-coming-for-your-job-its-coming?r=alhs&utm_medium=ios

“尽管大企业拥有诸多优势，但我认为个人创业者与微型企业的崛起是一个真实且持久的趋势。一本让我反复思考的书是阿尔弗雷德·钱德勒的《看得见的手》，它讲述了现代资本主义的兴起史。钱德勒认为，铁路和电报催生了大量需要大企业管理的销售与库存信息。这项工作需要职业经理人。于是，领薪的管理层级制度诞生了。

但AI和其他数字平台则不同；它们擅长综合已生成的信息。如果说铁路发明了现代组织架构图，那么AI原生企业正在发明一种反组织架构图——一种协调工作越来越多由模型和数字平台完成，而非层层人类经理的企业。当新企业不再需要大公司积累的官僚体系时，它们的薪资支出可以保持精简，而收益却变得庞大。

因此，我们经历了从无需中央控制系统的‘看不见的手’（资本主义通过价格协调），到经理人的‘看得见的手’（通过价格协调以控制信息洪流），再到‘看不见的在线人手’——包括AI在内的数字平台，让个体经营者能以更少的人力完成更多工作。”

https://open.substack.com/pub/derekthompson/p/ai-isnt-coming-for-your-job-its-coming?r=alhs&utm_medium=ios

2018年，摩根大通 CEO 杰米·戴蒙在一次内部会议上提到，他用来评估复杂业务场景的工具，竟然是一个源自空战的理论模型。

这个模型就是 OODA 循环。

OODA 循环，全称是 Observe-Orient-Decide-Act（观察-定向-决策-行动）循环。

由美国空军上校 约翰·博伊德 在20世纪70年代初提出，最初用于解释战斗机飞行员在空战中如何快速做出正确判断。

对抗中，速度不是全部，但循环速度的差异足以决定胜负。

感觉未来大模型或 AI 组织的竞争也是这样，谁自我迭代循环的快，谁才能赢。

items.text:
Andrej Karpathy, ex-Director of AI at Tesla:

"suddenly everyone is a programmer because everyone speaks natural language like English."

that one sentence is why cyril's post is even possible. "bachelor's in computer science required" was a real gate back when the only way to talk to a machine was a language you needed a degree to learn. karpathy's point is that the interface changed. you now program the model in english.

so what gets filtered for changed too. the post says portfolio beats credential in 2026, and that is the same idea from the other side. when the entry skill is describing what you want and building until it works, a degree stops being proof of anything and three shipped projects start being the proof.

the stack cyril lists, python, apis, embeddings, rag, agents, deployment, is not a cs curriculum. it is what you pick up while building those three projects, in english, with the tools karpathy is describing. ai engineering roles grew 143% year over year, per the post, because the door got wider, not because the work got easier.

the gate didn't fall because someone was nice. it fell because the language of the machine became one almost everyone already speaks. that is who gets to hold ai now: whoever finishes something real.
items.text_zh:
安德烈·卡帕斯（Andrej Karpathy），前特斯拉AI总监：

“突然之间，人人都成了程序员，因为人人都能说英语这样的自然语言。”

正是这句话，让西里尔的帖子成为可能。“要求计算机科学学士学位”曾是一道真正的门槛，因为当时与机器交流的唯一方式是一门需要学位才能学会的语言。卡帕斯的观点是：交互界面变了。现在，你用英语对模型编程。

因此，筛选标准也随之改变。帖子说，2026年作品集胜过学历证书，这从另一个角度印证了同一个道理。当入门技能变成描述你想要什么、然后动手构建直到成功时，学位就不再是能力的证明，而三个已上线的项目开始成为真正的凭证。

西里尔列出的技术栈——Python、API、嵌入、RAG、智能体、部署——并不是计算机科学的课程体系。而是你在用英语、借助卡帕斯所描述的工具、完成那三个项目的过程中，自然而然掌握的东西。据帖子称，AI工程岗位同比增长了143%，不是因为工作变简单了，而是因为门槛变宽了。

这道门槛的消失，不是因为有人大发善心。而是因为机器的语言变成了几乎人人都能说的语言。现在，谁能真正做出东西来，谁就能掌握AI。

用了一阵子各种 AI Agent 产品后，我逐渐意识到一个容易被忽略的底层差异——沙箱里到底装了什么，这件事比 AI 多聪明更重要。
桌面 Agent vs 云端 Agent，安全模型天生不同
桌面 Agent（你笔记本上跑的那种）没什么边界感可言。它能直接读你本地文件，随手抓你的环境变量，崩了你就点个重试——一切都建立在「你是这台电脑的主人」这个前提上，安全边界和执行环境是混在一起的。
但云端 Agent 完全不是这么回事。它跑在共享服务器上，执行的是 LLM 动态生成的未知代码，随时可能面临提示词注入或恶意攻击。在这种环境里，沙箱的信条只能有一条：给你执行力，不给你权限。
一个设计良好的云端 Agent，沙箱里只应该有纯粹的运算能力——跑代码、执行命令。所有涉及身份认证、API 密钥、数据库密码、甚至计费扣款的敏感操作，都应该由宿主层拦截、校验、代理执行。Slack 的 token 不在沙箱里，沙箱只能通过宿主发起一次经过认证的 Slack 调用。Gmail 的 OAuth 凭据不在沙箱里，沙箱只能让宿主替它去查邮件。
这意味着什么？哪怕 LLM 生成了一段恶意代码，它拿不到你的密钥，也接触不到你的资产。
更隐蔽的坑：Token 都烧在了搭环境上
安全隔离听起来很好，但如果实现得粗糙，会带来另一个灾难——Token 黑洞。
我亲身体验过某些产品：想让它帮我做一份 PPT，结果它花光了所有 Token 去 pip install python-pptx、装依赖、调版本兼容性、处理报错、再重试……等环境终于搭完，Token 额度没了，PPT 还没开始做。你什么都没得到，但这一轮的配额已经烧光了。
这种情况的根本原因在于：沙箱的初始环境是一张白纸，每个任务都要从零开始配置运行时。开发团队把「隔离」理解成了「什么都别放」，结果用户承担了所有构建成本的代价。
Creao AI 的做法：隔离但不裸奔
Creao AI 在这个问题上抓住了关键平衡——它的沙箱也是云端隔离的，也严格遵守「沙箱不持密钥」的安全模型，但沙箱初始环境是预配置好常用工具链的。做 PPT 的环境现成可用，做数据分析的库已经装好，连 Gmail 连接器自带配好的 Google Cloud Project、Gmail API 开箱即用。你不需要先花几十步对话去搭一个能干活的环境，上来就是干活本身。
这个差别本质上是产品团队对「什么该放在沙箱里、什么不该」的理解深度：
不放密钥、不放权限、不放身份——这是安全底线
但放工具链、放运行时、放已验证的依赖——这是产品良心
好的云端 Agent，应该是你打开就能干活，而不是先花一半配额给它装修办公室。Creao AI 在这条线上画得很清楚：不该进沙箱的绝不进去，但该进去的它早就替你备好了。

people still say LLMs are "just matrix multiplications" (the AI version of saying humans are "just electrochemical signals"... technically true, completely uninformative)

this LW post from 2023 made the case against reductionism with what was available then: a small transformer learning discrete Fourier transforms to solve modular addition, evidence of internal board representations in Othello-trained models, ~50% on the MATH competition dataset after fine-tuning

three years later the delta is so hard to overstate: GPT-5 now scores 100% on AIME 2026 (the benchmark that replaced MATH because MATH got saturated), GPT-5.5 scores 95% on ARC-AGI (a benchmark specifically designed to resist pattern matching and test fluid reasoning), frontier models resolve real GitHub issues end-to-end at ~80% on SWE-bench

and there's now a growing body of research and also AI neolabs specifically studying whether LLMs build internal spatial world models, and finding evidence that they do implicitly encode spatial and temporal relationships

the "just pattern matching" crowd keeps moving the goalposts as each previous goal gets cleared 🙄

though I do think that at some point everyone will convergre to an explanation that something real is happening inside these systems, even if we don't fully understand what

http://lesswrong.com/posts/PwfwZ2LeoLC4FXyDA/against-llm-reductionism
items.text_zh:
人们仍说大语言模型“不过是矩阵乘法”（这就像说人类“不过是电化学信号”……技术上正确，但毫无信息量）。

这篇2023年的LW文章用当时已有的证据反驳了还原论：一个小型Transformer通过学习离散傅里叶变换来解决模加法、在奥赛罗训练模型中存在内部棋盘表征的证据、微调后在MATH竞赛数据集上达到约50%的准确率。

三年后的差距简直难以言表：GPT-5在AIME 2026上已取得100%的分数（该基准取代了因饱和而被淘汰的MATH），GPT-5.5在ARC-AGI上达到95%（一个专门设计来对抗模式匹配、测试流体推理的基准），前沿模型在SWE-bench上以约80%的成功率端到端解决真实的GitHub问题。

而且现在有越来越多的研究以及AI新实验室专门探究大语言模型是否构建内部空间世界模型，并发现证据表明它们确实隐式编码了空间和时间关系。

“不过是模式匹配”的那群人，每当上一个目标被攻克，就不断把球门往后移🙄。

不过我确实认为，到了某个时候，所有人都会达成共识：这些系统内部确实在发生某种真实的事情，即使我们尚未完全理解它是什么。

http://lesswrong.com/posts/PwfwZ2LeoLC4FXyDA/against-llm-reductionism

items.text:
Prefill & decode in LLM inference.

Have you ever noticed that the first token from an LLM always takes a moment to appear? But the subsequent tokens stream out smoothly?

That pause isn't a network lag, but rather it's a structural property of how LLMs fundamentally work.

Inference happens in two phases that share the same model and the same code path, but the workload looks completely different in each, with different bottlenecks.

> Prefill stage starts when you submit a prompt.

The model processes every input token in one parallel pass, computing Q, K, and V for all of them at once.

Attention runs as a matrix multiplication, and the GPU chips run at high utilization, doing fast math.

Prefill is compute-bound, and the metric that captures it is time-to-first-token (TTFT).

> Decode stage starts once the first token is out.

To generate the next one, the model only computes Q, K, and V for that single new token, because everything before it is already cached.

So the model loops one token per forward pass, multiplying a single query against the cached keys instead of a full matrix. This makes the inference fast due to the tiny computation.

But the GPU still has to load every weight and every cached entry from memory to do that tiny computation, so the bottleneck flips and compute sits idle while memory bandwidth becomes the limiting factor.

Decode is memory-bound, and the metric that captures it is inter-token latency (ITL).

GPU utilization peaks during prefill and drops sharply during decode because memory, not compute, is the bottleneck in the second phase.

Throwing more compute at a slow-streaming model often does nothing because the fix for memory-bound workloads is faster memory or a smaller cache, not more FLOPs.

Long contexts feel disproportionately slow because the KV cache grows with every token, and every decode step has to read all of it.

But maintaining the cache is an important optimization since it makes decoding viable.

- Without KV cache, every new token would force a recomputation of attention over the entire growing sequence.
- With KV cache, the cache is built once during prefill, then grows by exactly one entry per decode step, with existing entries reused rather than recomputed.

The cache lives in GPU memory and grows linearly with sequence length, so a 13B model roughly requires 1 MB per token, which means a 4K context consumes 4 GB of VRAM on the cache alone.

The entire field is now optimizing around this constraint with quantized caches, sliding windows, grouped-query attention, and PagedAttention, while DeepSeek's V4 series goes further and redesigns attention itself so the cache stays small from the start.

The practical takeaway is that when someone says their model feels slow, the first question is whether it's slow to start or slow to stream.

Slow to start means prefill and a compute bottleneck, while slow to stream means decode and a memory bottleneck.

The article below is a first-principles guide to LLM inference that walks through everything between your prompt and the streamed response, covering tokenization, embeddings, attention, the prefill and decode split, KV caching, and quantization.

It will give you a complete mental model of how inference actually works under the hood.

Read it below.

## LLM 推理中的预填充与解码

你是否注意过，LLM 的第一个 token 总是需要片刻才能出现？但后续的 token 却能流畅地流式输出？

这个停顿并非网络延迟，而是 LLM 根本工作方式的结构性属性。

推理分为两个阶段，它们共享相同的模型和代码路径，但每个阶段的工作负载截然不同，瓶颈也各不相同。

> 当你提交提示词时，预填充阶段开始。

模型在一个并行步骤中处理所有输入 token，一次性计算它们的 Q、K 和 V。

注意力机制以矩阵乘法的方式运行，GPU 芯片以高利用率运行，进行快速数学运算。

预填充是计算密集型的，衡量它的指标是首 token 时间 (TTFT)。

> 一旦第一个 token 输出，解码阶段开始。

为了生成下一个 token，模型只计算这单个新 token 的 Q、K 和 V，因为之前的所有内容都已缓存。

因此，模型每次前向传播循环处理一个 token，将单个查询与缓存的键相乘，而不是进行完整的矩阵运算。这使得推理速度很快，因为计算量很小。

但 GPU 仍然需要从内存中加载每个权重和每个缓存条目来执行这个微小的计算，因此瓶颈发生了翻转，计算单元闲置，而内存带宽成为限制因素。

解码是内存密集型的，衡量它的指标是 token 间延迟 (ITL)。

GPU 利用率在预填充期间达到峰值，并在解码期间急剧下降，因为在第二阶段，内存而非计算是瓶颈。

向一个流式输出缓慢的模型投入更多算力通常无济于事，因为解决内存密集型工作负载的方法是更快的内存或更小的缓存，而不是更多的 FLOPs。

长上下文感觉异常缓慢，因为 KV 缓存会随着每个 token 增长，并且每个解码步骤都必须读取全部缓存。

但维护缓存是一项重要的优化，因为它使解码成为可能。

- 如果没有 KV 缓存，每个新 token 都将迫使对整个不断增长的序列重新计算注意力。
- 有了 KV 缓存，缓存会在预填充期间一次性构建，然后每个解码步骤仅增加一个条目，现有条目被重用而非重新计算。

缓存位于 GPU 内存中，并随序列长度线性增长，因此一个 13B 模型大约每个 token 需要 1 MB，这意味着一个 4K 上下文仅缓存一项就消耗 4 GB 的显存。

整个领域现在都在围绕这个约束进行优化，采用量化缓存、滑动窗口、分组查询注意力和 PagedAttention，而 DeepSeek 的 V4 系列更进一步，重新设计了注意力机制本身，使缓存从一开始就保持较小。

实际要点是，当有人说他们的模型感觉慢时，首先要问的问题是：是启动慢还是流式输出慢。

启动慢意味着预填充和计算瓶颈，而流式输出慢则意味着解码和内存瓶颈。

下面的文章是一份 LLM 推理的第一性原理指南，它详细介绍了从你的提示词到流式响应之间的所有环节，涵盖了分词、嵌入、注意力机制、预填充与解码的划分、KV 缓存以及量化。

它将为你提供一个完整的思维模型，让你了解推理在底层是如何实际工作的。

请阅读下文。

Cat Wu, Head of Product for Claude Code and Cowork, Anthropic:

"for everyone's job, there's always this percentage of it that's really tedious. for me, it's responding to emails."

that line is the whole premise of this guide, from the person who runs cowork. sairahul1's number is 60%: the share of a knowledge worker's day spent on production that doesn't need their brain. cowork doesn't make you faster at it, it removes you from it.

the part most people miss is what's left. wu's hope is that the agent takes the tedious slice so everyone has room for the things only they can build. the post says the same in other words: the bottleneck stops being production and becomes you, your judgment, your decisions.

the endgame in the guide, the 7am briefing and the self-running day, is exactly where she says cowork is headed: "the next big thing is proactivity. claude understands what you work on, and just sets up some of these automations for you."

one caveat she's clear on: you can't manage agents if you can't do the job yourself. you still have to know why the agent got it wrong. the folder, the templates, the about-me files, that is you teaching a coworker, not outsourcing the thinking.

items.text:
The biggest AI advantage isn't owning more GPUs.

It's building better loops.

Jane Street's AI cluster is massive.

4,032 Blackwell GPUs.

56 racks.

140kW per cabinet.

Water piped directly onto the chips.

Most people will look at those numbers and think that's the secret.

It isn't.

As Ron Minsky put it, everyone is competing for the same compute.

Hardware is becoming accessible.

Leverage comes from what your systems do once that compute is available.

The companies that win won't necessarily have the biggest clusters.

They'll build the best workflows on top of them.

That's exactly the shift I break down in the article below.
items.text_zh:
最大的AI优势不在于拥有更多GPU。

而在于构建更好的工作流。

简街的AI集群规模庞大。

4,032块Blackwell GPU。

56个机架。

每个机柜功耗140千瓦。

水直接泵送到芯片上。

大多数人看到这些数字会认为这就是秘诀。

其实不然。

正如Ron Minsky所说，所有人都在争夺同样的算力。

硬件正变得触手可及。

真正的杠杆在于，一旦算力就绪，你的系统能做什么。

最终胜出的公司未必拥有最大的集群。

而是能在集群之上构建出最佳工作流。

这正是我在下文中剖析的核心转变。

2025 was the year of AGENTS
2026 is the year of the HARNESS

Everyone is building agents. Orchestrators, tool calls, memory layers, multi-step reasoning. The demos are impressive.

But demos do not have real users. Demos do not have real costs. Demos do not fail at 3am.

That is what production is for.
The Agent Harness is the infrastructure layer that sits between your LLM and the real world.

It is not the model. It is not the prompt.

It manages your subagents, controls their context windows, routes tools to the right agents, tracks costs, handles failures, and keeps everything from falling apart when load hits.

Why you need it in the first place is covered in the previous article: https://x.com/kmeanskaran/status/2066139671412035728?s=20

The model is the easy part. Plugging in agents is the easy part. Making a system that holds up in real production situations requires actual engineering.

This article covers everything you need to get there.

Also a shoutout to @TejasKumar_ whose talk was a huge help in understanding the foundations of the Agent Harness. 
Beyond the content, the presentation skill and confidence were genuinely impressive.

Keep learning. Keep building.

2025年是智能体之年  
2026年是驾驭智能体之年  

每个人都在构建智能体。编排器、工具调用、记忆层、多步推理。演示效果令人印象深刻。  

但演示没有真实用户。演示没有真实成本。演示不会在凌晨三点崩溃。  

那才是生产环境的意义所在。  
智能体驾驭框架（Agent Harness）是位于你的大语言模型与现实世界之间的基础设施层。  

它不是模型。它不是提示词。  

它管理你的子智能体，控制它们的上下文窗口，将工具路由到正确的智能体，追踪成本，处理故障，并在负载来袭时防止一切崩溃。  

为何首先需要它，在上一篇文章中已有涵盖：https://x.com/kmeanskaran/status/2066139671412035728?s=20  

模型是简单的部分。接入智能体是简单的部分。构建一个能在真实生产环境中站得住脚的系统，需要真正的工程能力。

同时特别感谢 @TejasKumar_，他的演讲对理解智能体驾驭框架的基础提供了巨大帮助。

持续学习。持续构建。

Top 10 system design resources I still point working devs to:

1) Designing Data-Intensive Applications (Kleppmann) — real tradeoffs: logs vs DBs, consistency, stream processing.
2) Software Architecture: The Hard Parts (Ford/Richards) — how to choose, not just patterns; good on modularity and coupling.
3) Site Reliability Engineering (Google) — SLIs/SLOs, error budgets, incident response, capacity planning.
4) System Design Interview (Alex Xu) — fast reps; good for sketching APIs, storage, caching, sharding under time pressure.
5) Designing Distributed Systems (Brendan Burns) — Kubernetes patterns explained as general distributed system building blocks.
6) AWS Well-Architected Framework — concrete checklists for reliability, security, cost; useful even if you run on-prem.
7) Martin Fowler’s architecture articles (http://martinfowler.com) — bounded context, evolutionary architecture, integration patterns.
8) High Scalability blog (http://highscalability.com) — teardown posts; learn why teams picked queues, caches, and DBs in prod.
9) Jepsen analyses (http://jepsen.io) — teaches failure modes you only find at 3am: split brain, stale reads, bad retries.
10) Practice project: build a mini SaaS and run it — REST+DB, add Redis cache, background jobs, metrics/tracing, load test, then break it with chaos/fault injection

I remember seeing this from @FreyaHolmer  for the first time and going "wtf, I got gaslit". I've shown this to many of my programmer friends without math background and most of them were "wait, that's it?". Yes, that's literally it. Obviously only the surface of what math has to offer, but the same principles apply to all sorts of other notations. If you give the (pseudo) code next to it, nice code highlighting, with introspection, definition jumping, debugging, you make Math actually easy to understand and approachable - exactly what we did with programming languages over decades with all these nice tools we now have.
There's a reason some programming languages are more popular than others, but you can do most things with either. And I think the same lens explains math notation: it's not that the concepts are complex, it's that the compression rate is so high that most people bail the fuck out and think this stuff is super complex, when in reality it is not. The underlying principles are super easy once you approach them in a different format (like most of my programmer colleagues here did with approachable languages like JavaScript), it's all about the notation, abstractions, and tools used, and math manages to be the most compact and the most ugly at the same time to me (although I got more used to it over the years).
Programming languages in that same compact category failed hard, for a good reason, people avoid what is unpleasant to look at, read, and requires a big corpus of prerequisites and working memory. I'm actually kind of afraid to think about how many brilliant people avoided math purely because of the notation, not because of the complexity. My theory is that good math people aren't inherently smarter; they just parse and memorize these ugly symbols better or got used to them much earlier in brain development. You can see it clearly in the programming world, where way more people are comfortable writing pretty complicated code but would never touch the most basic math primitives.
It almost feels like math notation is compressed so hard that your brain has to do all the unfolding manually, you hold this huge unpacked state in your head just to work on it, and learning to do that is the hard part most people never push through, so they bail. But code itself has it unfolded for you already: explorable, debuggable, jump-to-definition, back and forth. Your brain doesn't have to hold the whole thing at once, so it can actually chunk it and reason about it much better. The fact that you can modify it and get instant computed feedback in a particular actual real-world use-case makes it much easier to burn an intuition into your brain. Programming runs at a high bandwidth by default, some say too verbose; I say it's an equilibrium evolved over decades, and the proof is the millions of programmers worldwide.
items.text_zh:
我第一次看到 @FreyaHolmer 的这个观点时，心想"什么鬼，我是不是被忽悠了"。后来我把它展示给许多没有数学背景的程序员朋友，大多数人反应是"等等，就这么简单？"。没错，真的就这么简单。显然这只是数学的冰山一角，但同样的原理适用于各种其他符号体系。如果你在旁边配上（伪）代码、漂亮的代码高亮、支持内省、定义跳转和调试功能，数学就变得真正易于理解和亲近——这正是我们几十年来对编程语言所做的，才有了现在这些好用的工具。

有些编程语言比其他语言更受欢迎是有原因的，但大多数事情用哪种语言都能完成。我认为用同样的视角可以解释数学符号：问题不在于概念本身复杂，而在于压缩率太高，导致大多数人直接放弃，觉得这些东西超级复杂，而实际上并非如此。一旦你用不同的形式去接触（就像我大多数程序员同事用 JavaScript 这类易上手的语言一样），底层原理其实非常简单。关键在于符号、抽象和工具的使用，而数学在我看来同时做到了最紧凑和最丑陋（虽然这些年我也逐渐习惯了）。

编程语言中那些同样追求紧凑的尝试都失败了，这有其充分理由——人们会避开那些看起来不悦目、读起来不顺畅、需要大量前置知识和工作记忆的东西。我甚至有点害怕去想，有多少杰出的人仅仅因为符号体系而避开了数学，而不是因为复杂度本身。我的理论是，数学好的人并非天生更聪明；他们只是更擅长解析和记忆这些丑陋的符号，或者在大脑发育早期就习惯了它们。这在编程世界里看得一清二楚：更多人能轻松写出相当复杂的代码，却绝不会碰最基础的数学原语。

这几乎就像数学符号被压缩得太狠，你的大脑必须手动完成所有解压工作，你得在脑子里维持这个巨大的展开状态才能继续工作，而学会做这件事正是大多数人永远无法突破的难点，所以他们放弃了。但代码本身已经为你展开了：可探索、可调试、可跳转到定义、可来回查看。你的大脑不必一次性容纳全部内容，因此能更好地分块处理并推理。你可以修改代码并在实际用例中立即获得计算反馈，这大大有助于在脑中建立直觉。编程默认以高带宽运行，有人说过于冗长；我认为这是几十年来演化出的平衡态，而证明就是全球数百万程序员的存在。

items.text:
good LW post on productivity techniques (link below)
went through it and checked what I actually do vs. what didn't stick

works for me
- task capture: I log every ~15-30min of work hours in my calendar and have AI generate an end-of-day summary
- underschedule: a deliberate weekly block of unplanned time (tho I got here through hypercontrol work, not productivity literature)
- focus on the wildly important: "only hell yes" rule (will write a separate post on my prioritization framework at some point...)
- rest / solitude / productive meditation: honestly my favorite category haha (jacuzzi, weighted blanket, sensory walks, breathwork, jazz clubs, baths, etc etc...)
- also: CBT and EMDR, coaching calls, strength + mobility + endurance 3x+/week, and working with a human personal assistant (not AI!)

didn't stick
- app blockers (SelfControl, Freedom)
- spaced repetition software (tried but abandoned)

the thing the post almost gets to but doesn't quite say: the post ends with "don't make yourself crazy" and flags that rigid scheduling fails where flexible planning survives
what I learned through hypercontrol work is that the urge to systematize everything can be anxiety in disguise rather than genuine productivity
so I spent quite a few years identifying which control patterns were net positive and keeping only those...

http://lesswrong.com/posts/P3zrurj5hHKFKDL3M/productivity-working-towards-a-summary-of-what-we-know
items.text_zh:
一篇关于生产力技巧的优秀LW帖子（链接见下）
我通读了一遍，核对了自己实际在做的，以及哪些方法没能坚持下来

对我有效的方法
- 任务记录：每工作15-30分钟就在日历上记录一笔，让AI生成当日总结
- 留出余量：每周刻意留出一段未安排的时间（不过我是通过高压管控工作法悟到的，并非来自生产力文献）
- 聚焦真正重要的事："非绝对肯定就拒绝"原则（之后会专门写一篇关于我的优先级框架的文章……）
- 休息/独处/有效冥想：说实话这是我最喜欢的类别哈哈（按摩浴缸、重力毯、感官散步、呼吸练习、爵士俱乐部、泡澡等等……）
- 此外还有：认知行为疗法和眼动脱敏与再处理、教练辅导、每周3次以上的力量+柔韧+耐力训练，以及配备真人助理（不是AI！）

没能坚持的方法
- 应用拦截器（SelfControl、Freedom）
- 间隔重复软件（试过但放弃了）

那篇文章几乎触及但未明确说出的要点：文章结尾提到"别把自己逼疯"，并指出僵化的日程安排终将失败，而灵活的计划才能持久
通过高压管控工作法，我领悟到：将一切系统化的冲动，可能并非真正的生产力，而是焦虑的伪装
所以我花了好几年时间，识别出哪些管控模式是净收益，并只保留这些模式……

items.text:
This paper completely changed how I think about assembling a RAG pipeline:

Define the nodes -> List candidates for each -> Run them on your dataset -> Keep the winner -> Move to the next node

Here is the 5-step blueprint:

Nodes: the pipeline is split into stages - query expansion, retrieval, augmenter, reranker, prompt maker.

Candidates: each node gets a set of interchangeable modules - BM25, vectordb, hybrids, rerankers.

Greedy per node: you optimize nodes one at a time, locking the best module before moving on.

Two metrics: retrieval is measured separately from generation, so you see exactly where quality leaks.

On your own data: the optimum is searched on your corpus, not a foreign leaderboard - the best module for Wikipedia QA fails on domain docs.

Key insight: the best RAG pipeline is not picked from a benchmark, it is found by search on your own dataset.

Five pipeline stages, each with a pool of interchangeable modules, and the loop assembles the winning combination on its own.

Read this, then check the article below.
items.text_zh:
这篇论文彻底改变了我对构建 RAG 管线的思考方式：

定义节点 → 为每个节点列出候选方案 → 在你的数据集上运行 → 保留优胜者 → 进入下一个节点

以下是五步蓝图：

节点：管线被拆分为多个阶段——查询扩展、检索、增强器、重排序器、提示生成器。

候选方案：每个节点都有一组可互换的模块——BM25、向量数据库、混合检索、重排序器。

逐节点贪心优化：每次只优化一个节点，锁定最佳模块后再继续。

两个指标：检索与生成分开衡量，这样你能准确看到质量损耗发生在哪里。

基于你自己的数据：最优方案是在你的语料库上搜索得出的，而不是依赖外部的排行榜——在维基百科问答上表现最佳的模块，在领域文档上却会失效。

关键洞察：最佳的 RAG 管线不是从基准测试中挑选出来的，而是通过在你自己的数据集上搜索找到的。

五个管线阶段，每个阶段都有一组可互换的模块池，循环会自动组装出获胜的组合。

先读这个，再看下面的文章。

You don’t need a complicated memory. Just a few independent, mutually exclusive files that skills can reference on demand.

In most cases, it’s enough to load these progressively and mention them in the agents file.

The exception is sequential memories for a given project. In that case, it’s useful to keep a ledger of memories, decisions, and similar records - which is what PM OS has in versions 2 and up.
items.text_zh:

items.text:
S3 has been around forever and in recent times, AWS has kept expanding what you can do with it. Recently S3 Files was announced and it has a lot of use cases where it makes sense. One typical pattern with Lambda functions is downloading objects to /tmp, processing them, and uploading the result, plus all the boilerplate for transfers, capacity checks, and cleanup. Amazon S3 Files takes a different angle.

The new approach is mounting an S3 bucket directly as a local file system, so your function just reads and writes at a path like /mnt/data and sync happens behind the scenes. The transfer code disappears and the /tmp size limit stops being a constraint you have to design around.

Sharan Sutrapu shows three real cases including a shared workspace for multi-agent AI, thumbnail generation, and a CSV to Parquet pipeline. Check it out!

https://lckhd.eu/Tpx5K5

#AWS #S3 #S3Files #Lambda #Serverless

新方法是将 S3 存储桶直接挂载为本地文件系统，这样你的函数只需在 /mnt/data 这样的路径下读写文件，同步操作在后台自动完成。传输代码消失了，/tmp 的大小限制也不再是你需要费心规避的约束。

Sharan Sutrapu 展示了三个实际案例，包括多智能体 AI 的共享工作空间、缩略图生成，以及 CSV 转 Parquet 的数据管道。快去看看吧！

items.text:
Boris Cherny, Head of Claude Code, Anthropic:

"you can define a stop hook that's like, if the tests don't pass, keep going. essentially it's like you can just make the model keep going until the thing is done."

that one config is the post's loop #1, straight from the person who built the tool. a stop hook fires every time the turn ends, so the work can't be called done until tests and lint go green. deterministic, zero effort, the loop most people skip.

cherny describes the verification loop in his own words too: for big changes his team spawns subagents to find every issue, one checking claude.md compliance, one combing git history, one hunting bugs, then five more subagents whose only job is to kill the false positives. a fresh clean-context critic catches what the builder talked itself past.

and the memory loop, in his words: if you see a mistake, you just tell claude to add it to claude.md, so next time it already knows. the correction outlives the session it happened in.

four loops, none exotic. each is a few lines of config or one instruction. seniors out-ship everyone else because they run all four at once, not because their model is smarter.
items.text_zh:
Boris Cherny, Anthropic 的 Claude Code 负责人：

"你可以定义一个停止钩子，比如：如果测试没通过，就继续。本质上，你可以让模型一直运行，直到任务完成。"

这个配置就是本文的循环 #1，直接来自该工具的构建者。每次回合结束时，停止钩子都会触发，因此只有在测试和 lint 检查全部通过后，工作才能算完成。确定性、零投入，这是大多数人跳过的循环。

Cherny 也用他自己的话描述了验证循环：对于重大变更，他的团队会派生子代理来查找所有问题——一个检查 claude.md 的合规性，一个梳理 git 历史，一个寻找 bug，然后再派五个子代理，它们的唯一任务就是消除误报。一个全新的、上下文干净的批评者能捕捉到构建者自己说服自己忽略的问题。

至于记忆循环，用他的话来说：如果你发现了一个错误，只需告诉 Claude 将其添加到 claude.md 中，这样下次它就已经知道了。这个修正会超越它发生的会话而持续存在。

四个循环，没有一个稀奇。每个只是几行配置或一条指令。资深开发者之所以能比其他人交付更多，是因为他们同时运行所有四个循环，而不是因为他们的模型更聪明。

items.text: must-read

Claude Tag is a warning shot. 

Every AI vendor is about to want to own the one thing you can't afford to rent: your company's context.

Tag it in Slack and it'll start learning everything: your clients, your workflows, the stuff that normally lives in one person's head. Within months it'll be the smartest entity in your company about your company. 

It's a gift and the trap in one move. The smarter it gets, the more of your business lives inside a system you don't own. You can swap the model anytime sure. But you can't swap the memory of how your company runs once it's piled up in someone else's house.

Letting the same vendor sell you the model AND own your context is how you end up renting your own company back from them.

So you've really got two options.

Run Claude Tag and let your context collect inside their walls.

or

Build your own company brain. Internal if you've got the engineers, or managed and built for you by a team that does this all day, which is what we do at Single Brain.

Either rent your intelligence or own the brain yourself.
items.text_zh:
Claude Tag 是一记警告。

每一家 AI 供应商都即将想要拥有你租不起的东西：你公司的上下文。

在 Slack 里标记它，它就会开始学习一切：你的客户、你的工作流程、那些通常只存在于某个人脑子里的东西。几个月内，它就会成为你公司里最了解你公司的实体。

这是一份礼物，也是一个陷阱，一举两得。它越聪明，你的业务就越会存在于一个你不拥有的系统里。当然，你可以随时更换模型。但一旦你公司的运作方式堆积在别人家里，你就无法更换那段记忆。

让同一个供应商既卖给你模型，又拥有你的上下文，这就是你最终从他们那里把自己公司租回来的方式。

所以，你实际上有两个选择。

运行 Claude Tag，让你的上下文在他们的围墙内积累。

或者

建立你自己的公司大脑。如果你有工程师，就内部搭建；或者由一支整天做这件事的团队为你管理和构建——这就是我们在 Single Brain 做的事情。

要么租用你的智能，要么自己拥有大脑。

items.text:
Here is a condensed, high-impact version of the post:

Discover -> Hand off -> Verify -> Persist -> Schedule

This 12-page PDF completely changed how I build agentic systems. Here is the 5-step blueprint:

Discovery: The loop reads CI, issues, and commits to find what's worth fixing.

Handoff: Each finding gets an isolated git worktree so parallel agents never collide.

Verification: A second agent - built to assume the code is broken, reviews the work.

Persistence: Results land on disk, never in a temporary context window.

Scheduling: Automation fires the entire process on a timer, making it a true loop.

The key insight: An agent grading its own work always praises it. You need that second agent to say "no."

Read it now, then explore the article below.
items.text_zh:
发现 → 移交 → 验证 → 持久化 → 调度

这份12页的PDF彻底改变了我构建智能体系统的方式。以下是五步蓝图：

**发现**：循环读取CI、议题和提交记录，找出值得修复的内容。

**移交**：每个发现结果获得独立的Git工作树，确保并行智能体永不冲突。

**验证**：第二个智能体——预设代码存在缺陷——对工作进行审查。

**持久化**：结果写入磁盘，绝不留在临时上下文窗口中。

**调度**：自动化机制按定时器触发整个流程，形成真正的循环。

关键洞察：让智能体自我评分，它总会自我褒扬。你需要第二个智能体来说"不"。

At USV, we’ve long been students of the cycles of technology development and deployment, and the way in which value accrues at different layers at different points in the cycle. 

In the early 2000s, after the deployment of the physical internet, our belief was that value would accrue at the application layer. In the early 2010s, after the invention of bitcoin, our belief was that value would accrue in open source protocols below the application layer.  

Today, after the invention and deployment of AI foundation models, the question is: will all value accrue to the models, or to a broad ecosystem around them?

This idea that the agentic coding workflow should be three models, an orchestrator, executor, and code reviewer, is pretty broken imo.

The problem is, going multi-model isn't that revolutionary, if you're using only one agent at the execution layer.

Most complex problems aren't uniformly complex, so using one model at the execution layer means you're often using far more thinking depth, and tokens than you need.

I've been experimenting with a new agentic coding workflow, and I think the key aha moment I had is realizing that one model at the execution layer, will pretty much always mean, using way more tokens than you have to, to get the same result.
items.text_zh:
我认为那种将智能体编码工作流设计为三个模型（编排器、执行器和代码审查器）的想法相当有问题。

问题在于，如果执行层只使用一个智能体，那么采用多模型架构其实并不具有革命性意义。

大多数复杂问题并非均匀分布其复杂度，因此在执行层使用单一模型意味着你常常会消耗远超实际所需的思考深度和token数量。

我一直在尝试一种新的智能体编码工作流，而关键顿悟在于：在执行层使用单一模型，几乎必然意味着为了达成相同结果，你会消耗远超必要的token量。

items.text:
/loop and /goal do not validate your work.
They amplify whatever validation you give them.

The real problem: the agent never stops and reasons.

It tries. Fails. Tries something else. Fails again.
Try try try try try. Never once does it stops for:

"Wait. I tried that three times and it failed the same way. What is actual pattern in that failure?"

It's a hamster wheel with better insulation.

The fix: every N cycles, force a reasoning break.
Not more code. Not another tool call.
A blank window, where the model must analyze
what has been tried, why it failed, and propose
one concrete theory before the next attempt.

If your loop never stops to reason, 
it's not iterating. It's thrashing.
items.text_zh:
`/loop` 和 `/goal` 并不会验证你的工作——它们只会放大你赋予它们的验证逻辑。

真正的问题在于：智能体从不停下来思考。

它尝试，失败；换种方式再试，再次失败。
不断尝试、尝试、再尝试。它从未停下来问过：

"等等，这个方法我已经试了三次，每次都以同样的方式失败。这些失败背后真正的规律是什么？"

这就像一个加了更好隔音材料的仓鼠滚轮。

解决方案：每经过 N 个循环，强制插入一次推理中断。
不是写更多代码，也不是调用另一个工具。
而是一个空白窗口，让模型必须分析：
已经尝试过什么、为什么失败，并在下一次尝试前提出一个具体的理论。

如果你的循环从不停下来思考，
那它就不是在迭代，而是在空转。

items.text:
本地用vLLM部署GLM-5.2的速度终于上来了! 

好消息终于轮到本地部署 GLM-5.2 了! 大家都知道 GLM-5.2 这次是自带了MTP头的, 可以进行推测性解码. 

但是, 这个只适用于bf16原始精度的GLM-5.2, 而这玩意原始精度要到1.5TB, 本地跑的很少有富到这个程度的, 所以大家都用各种量化版本, 毕竟4bit量化就只要430GB了.

问题这就来了, 由于 GLM-5.2 的 MTP 采用了非常特殊的 DSA (动态稀疏注意力), 导致目前几个推理引擎 (llama.cpp, vLLM, mlx) 都无法支持. 

其中 llama.cpp, mlx 是完全没办法开 MTP, vLLM 只支持FP8精度的.

而SGLang 没事哈, SGLang 架构比较屌上来就支持同一个计算流使用混合精度. 所以直接用 GLM-5.2-W4AFP8 就行. 

所以回到这几个不支持的推理引擎, 大部分的量化版本 GLM-5.2 开了 MTP 反而会掉速度. 甚至有的量化版本直接把MTP部分给砍了(mlx). 

而社区作者dnhkng搞了个缝合方法, 最终搞出了 GLM-5.2-AWQ-INT4-FP8-MTP-delta, 即 底座用 INT4（走 Marlin 算子）+ MTP 用 FP8（保持精度）同时还能让vLLM 支持. 速度从原来的 2 token/s 直接飙升到了 43.39 token/s (绑定NUMA+MTP-3)

所以目前位置 SGLang 和 vLLM (魔改版)都能直接火力全开跑带MTP的 GLM-5.2了. 而 llama.cpp和mlx用户还需要再等等. 社区还在弄.

这个作者的blog (过程极其精彩, 有不少优化技巧): http://dnhkng.github.io/posts/gh200-benchmarking-part-3-glm52/

items.text:
推荐这篇文章，Flask 作者 Armin Ronacher 写了这两天我看到最诚实的 loops 反思。之前两篇都在讲 loop 怎么搭、工程怎么落地，这篇问了一个没人敢问的问题：loop 写出来的代码你真的喜欢吗？如果你在用 AI 写代码，这篇可能会让你停下来想一下。

即将到来的 Loop

我不再给 Claude 写 prompt 了。我跑着一些 loop，它们负责给 Claude 写 prompt 并决定做什么。我的工作是写 loop。

— Boris Cherny

过去几个月，我看到越来越多的人在 coding agent 之上构建一些感觉上跟"直接用 coding agent"有本质区别的东西。模式到处都一样：任务被放进某种队列，机器捡起来、尝试、停下来，然后 harness 判断那是不是真的结束。

如果不是，harness 继续同一个 session、注入另一条消息、用修改过的 context 启动一个新的 session、或者把任务发给另一台机器。任务在模型自己本该说"我做完了"的那个点之后，继续活着。

我想这种 loop 想到自己都不好意思承认。

每个 coding agent 内部已经有一个 agent loop 了。模型调用工具、整合结果、再调用工具、读文件、改文件、跑测试、最终生成答案。那个 loop 我们已经相当熟悉了。另一种 loop 是 harness 级别的 loop：agent loop 之外的 loop。那个 loop 也不是新的。从 Claude Code 早期我们就一直在做各种版本，但那个 loop 在 agentic engineering 中越来越重要，最近几周已经开始主导 Twitter discourse。

我还不擅长这个

我目前的状况是：对于我真正在意的代码，我还没怎么成功用过这种工作方式——而这恰好是我相当大一部分代码。

部分原因是品味，部分原因是控制。我对我想要的代码样子设了一个很高的标准，我想理解我交付的代码。在压力下，或者跟另一个人讨论时，我想能够解释清楚系统做了什么，而不是先让一个 clanker 解释给我听。显然，这种"想理解代码"的愿望是否会在几年后依旧存在，是一个问题。但现在，我还没有越过"理解对我来说很重要"这个阶段。

基于这个愿望，对于没有我关注时写出来的代码，尤其是由 loops 产生的代码，我感觉有些东西缺失了。当前模型倾向于产生过于防御性、过于复杂、推理过于局部的代码。它们避免强不变量。它们添加 fallback 而不是让坏状态变得不可能。它们重复代码、发明糟糕的抽象、用更多 machinery 掩盖不清晰的设计。更糟的是：我几乎看不到这方面有什么进步。如果有什么变化的话，我觉得我们可能还在往错误的方向走。至少以我的品味，当前像 Claude Code with ultracode 这样的无人值守 harness 产出的代码，比去年秋天我们产出的还要差。因为 Claude Code 加 Fable 会连续不停地在一个问题上工作 30 分钟甚至更久，而过去这个过程会有更多人参与。

此外，一个众所周知的问题是模型倾向于观察到某个局部失败然后添加局部防御。Karpathy 提到他们"对异常感到极度恐惧"。在具有重要不变量的系统中，尤其是持久化数据格式或核心基础设施，正确的修复不是"处理每个异常情况"。正确的修复是让异常情况一开始就无法被表达或写入。但即便有大量人工引导，LLM 也不会自然地产生那种代码，而且即使代码自然地像那样产生了，它们仍然会试图处理现在已不可能的错误。

当你把这种行为放到 loops 后面时，你往往会放大它。如果每次迭代都添加一个小防御，系统会慢慢变得更不透明，同时表面看起来更健壮。你越放手，这种情况就越严重。当这样的工具交给没有清晰指导的初级开发者时，它还会教给他们非常糟糕的实践。因为如果你问他们为什么做所有这些，他们会令人信服地论证自己的做法。

Loop 在哪里有效

但与此同时，假装 loop 模式不管用也是不诚实的——它在某些领域已经好得惊人。

代码移植就是其中之一。已经有令人印象深刻的大规模自动化移植案例，包括报道中把 Bun 的部分代码从 Zig 移植到 Rust 的工作。我自己也成功用它把 MiniJinja 移植到了 Go。性能探索是另一个效果惊艳的场景。机器可以尝试实验、跑 benchmark、丢弃失败、继续搜索。安全扫描也自然适合，几乎任何类型的研究也一样：让系统探索一个复杂的问题空间然后汇报回来，不一定要提交持久化的代码。

这些场景的共性是：它们要么不生成新代码，而是转换已有代码；要么产生的代码有意不需要长期存活。它们要么产出 PoC 或想法，要么呈现发现，或者更像机械性的转换。

我相信，产出不需要长寿的 artifacts 的 loop，或者产出某种可清晰验证的机械性翻译的 loop，比 harness 机械性地衡量某个目标的一般能力更重要。很多成功的 loop 应用用另一个 LLM 作为 judge 或 orchestrator。机械性翻译场景可以用二元测试用例验证，但它也可以用 LLM 来评判！

Claude Code 在创建完整的实验性工作流并执行它们方面，变得越来越好。当然，它生成的代码是 slop，但那更多是模型的问题，而不是 harness 不能很好地判断工作流中的某一步是否带来了净改进或完成。

Harness 只需要一些信号让它能继续。不需要客观或二元——只需要足够有用来驱动下一次迭代。

我非常喜欢那些能把我日常中的无聊部分拿走的 loops——做实验、测量、给我灵感。

软件作为有机体

另一方面，用同样的 loop 方法来写持久化的代码，我还不觉得舒服。我喜欢的比喻是：从软件作为确定性机器，到软件作为有机体。

我成为一名软件工程师的环境鼓励我理解机器。总有一层你可以剥开来加深理解。不展现确定性可观测行为的机器也许被接受，但一般不被认为是最优的。在软件架构上，我认为追求更多的确定性而不是更少是可取的。同样，理解代码的能力一直是一个不可否认的目标。实践中并不总是可能，但我们仍然以写出好的代码为荣，使得即使是新工程师也能通过巧妙的架构在复杂的代码库中导航。在设计良好的系统上，总有一些工程师知道不变量在哪里，哪些部分是承重的，哪些改动是安全的。理想情况下所有这些都是有良好文档的。在缺乏这种理解的地方，通常被认为是需要改进的事情。

显然，那个理想一直都很紧张。许多软件系统，尤其是非常成功的系统，在工程师能让它保持干净的时期过后，常常变得太大、太动态、太依赖外部服务，无法装进任何人的脑袋。即使没有 LLM，我们在诊断分布式系统时也已经有点像医生了：观察症状、提出假设、"开更多检查"、尝试一些补救措施、再次观察。

但有了 LLM，我们正在沿着这个方向走得更远更快。我们用它们来写代码，也用它们来诊断和治疗。已经有大量工程师生活在这样一个世界里：生产问题发生后的第一步是让 clanker 读日志、提出根因、主动提出 patch。结果 patch 通常被另一台机器捡起来审查，有时甚至没有任何人工监督就合并到了 main。

显然这很强大，我不能否认它听起来很诱人。但屈服于这个想法，特别是随着人类监督越来越少，意味着接受我们可能无法再以同样的方式理解整个系统。我们治疗它、监控它、稳定它，但我们不一定理解它。

我毫不怀疑对于某些软件来说，这没问题。不是每一行代码都值得人类作者身份，而且过去也可能写过更差的代码。

但我希望所有软件都这样写吗？

你无法完全退出

非常令人不安的是，选择退出这个全机器驱动的未来可能不是一个选项。

安全是最清晰的例子。即使你不用 loops 来构建你的软件，别人也会用 loops 来攻击你的软件。攻击者会持续运行机器，即使不是攻击者，安全研究人员也会，而其中一些自动化工作会产生大量噪音但也会发现真正的问题。信号和噪音都会以如此大的规模涌向你，以至于你几乎不得不也扔一台机器来处理。

Daniel Stenberg 关于 curl 的 summer of bliss 的帖子是一个很好的例子，展示了维护者已经承受的压力。据我所知，AI 在 curl 的核心开发中并没有扮演重要角色。但尽管如此，维护者还是被报告淹没了——其中大部分是 AI 生成的。

如果攻击者和报告者都在 loop，防御者最终也需要 loop 才能跟上。也许不是直接写 patch，也许只是用来 triage 和复现——但压力会增加。

竞争也是一样。有些团队会通过原始速度超越其他团队。有些项目会突然加速，因为一个小团队搞清楚了如何有效编排机器。有些 startup 可以用五个人做到过去需要五十个人的事。有些人可能会直接把一台机器放在一个 loop 里对着你的产品，告诉它"把它做得像那个一样"。而如果他们的用户很开心，这真的重要吗？

不是所有软件都会受到同等影响。有些领域会惩罚草率，要求信任和责任，但很多软件生活在一个原始速度、快速实验和大面积覆盖至关重要的世界里。

建立新的依赖

最可怕的部分是，我们以新的方式变得依赖于这些新机器。软件一直依赖工具。我还记得我不得不为编译器付费的时候。这些新工具让人回想起那些创造软件需要真实成本的日子。但现在不再是一次性付款了——它是一种持续的依赖。不只是对钱包的依赖，还有认知依赖。

如果一个代码库由 loops 产生、由 loops 审查、由 loops 打补丁、由 loops 维护，当你不再能访问同等级别的系统时会发生什么？当某些贸易限制剥夺了对最强模型的访问时？如果只是成本变得不可接受呢？如果你和你的团队只是丧失了不用机器理解代码的最后一点能力呢？

我们可能会创建出不仅人类难以维护、而且把机器参与作为其维护模型前提的代码库。这已经在发生了！不是在所有地方都发生，甚至可能不是以被视为有问题的方式在发生，但我们看到越来越多。人们越来越多地合并他们不能完全解释的代码。人们失去了创建 issue 报告或在聊天中讨论事情的能力，而不借助 clanker 增强或改写他们的消息。太多人越来越依赖机器来总结或提供上下文。我越来越多地遇到通过 LLM 这个中间人与我交流的人。

再说一次，也许这甚至不一定是错的，但它对我们做事的方式是一个巨大的改变。

未来的 Harness

我毫不怀疑这就是方向，但朝着这个方向走需要我们在所有地方都改善我们的工具，而不只是在 coding agent 里。

仅仅编排更多的 loops 是不够的。更好的变更可视化或编排或 agent 不会恢复我们的理解。要么我们需要找到巧妙的方法把人拉回 loop，让 loop 的变更长期可读，要么我们需要找到更好的方法来组合这些越来越复杂的系统。

这也是我对 Pi 的角色的想法在变化的地方。Pi 一直很谨慎，我认为这种谨慎是好的。我不希望一个每一次交互都变成不受控制的机器 swarm、做出我无法跟上的变更的未来。我不希望 Pi 为了赢得"软件自己写自己"的竞赛而变成一个不可维护的混乱，我也不希望 Pi 推广这类工程。但与此同时，Pi 是一个 harness，而 harness 正处在人们运行这些新型实验的中心。

编码任务的任务队列、agent 编排、子 agent、持久化 session 会变得越来越重要。即使是我们这些有保留意见、没有盲目拥抱 loops 的人，也必须要开始做这些实验了。因为我们需要理解如何让这个未来有边界、可生存。

控制 Loop

正如你从这篇文章中读到的，我对这个未来非常不安。不是因为恐惧，而是因为基于对这项技术至今的经验而产生的谨慎。

采用 harness loop 的想法意味着 harness 决定工作何时完成。在 agent loop 中，模型最终说"完成"然后我审查。即使在那之前，我通常也在沿途引导。我参与其中，我喜欢在学习中前行。在 harness 操作的 loop 中，我不确定我的角色到底是什么。甚至"完成"信号也失去了所有意义，只是变成了传递给另一台机器进行评判的信息。我的角色被简化为一个信使。

今天，我不喜欢我看到的那种用这种方式构建的系统产生的代码，我也不喜欢与太多用 AI 辅助构建的软件交互。Loop 很强大，但它越来越多地移除责任，至少在当下它非常鼓励我们向机器投降。

然而，我毫不怀疑这个 loop 化的未来就是我们的未来——尽管我目前对此感到反感。我已经看到惊人小的团队以不可能的速度在构建，我看到代码库正在变成越来越模糊和混乱的有机体，只能由更多机器来诊断。这些代码库同时既有用又混乱。

所以我想我开始接受一个事实：问题不是我们会不会 loop——显然我们会的。也许问题是：在一个 loops 的未来里，我们如何不放弃判断，如何在其中保留良好工程的原则，如何确保负责任的人能够继续监督，如何重新思考我们架构代码的方式以在其中保持清醒。

原文：Armin Ronacher, "The Coming Loop", 2026-06-23
链接：https://lucumr.pocoo.org/2026/6/23/the-coming-loop/

I spent 20+ years following the future of Business Intelligence. Here's what I found. BI in 2026 is unrecognizable from where it started. The shift from dashboards to declarative stacks to agentic engineering changed everything. And yet, the fundamentals never moved.

If you want to bridge BI and DE, and build stacks that work with agents while staying true to what BI was always about, then here are 9 concepts to learn:

1. AI Reveals Why BI Still Matters. The hint: AI agents are blind to dashboards. They need the BI primitives: metrics, semantics, governance. Agents depend on them. https://www.rilldata.com/blog/ai-reveals-why-bi-still-matters-hint-its-not-dashboards

2. Has Self-Serve BI Finally Arrived Thanks to AI? After a year of trying MCPs and many more with a semantic-aware logical layer, AI acts on the promise, because agents autonomously understand business context beyond just SQL. https://www.ssp.sh/blog/self-service-bi-ai/

3. Building an Agent-Friendly, Local-First Analytics Stack. What agent-first BI actually looks like: local DuckDB + MotherDuck + Rill YAML metrics that LLMs can parse, reason about, and modify without breaking. https://www.rilldata.com/blog/building-an-agent-friendly-local-first-analytics-stack-with-motherduck-and-rill

4. BI-as-Code and the New Era of GenBI. What happens when dashboards live in YAML and SQL instead of proprietary UIs? LLMs can read, generate, and maintain them. This unlocks much faster iterations in production. https://www.rilldata.com/blog/bi-as-code-and-the-new-era-of-genbi

5. Why Pivot Tables Never Die. They've been the lingua franca of data exploration since 1989. Understanding why tells you something essential about how humans (and AI) actually interact with data. https://www.rilldata.com/blog/why-pivot-tables-never-die

6. The Rise of the Declarative Data Stack. The shift from imperative configs to Kubernetes-style YAML. The foundation everything else builds on. https://www.ssp.sh/blog/rise-of-declarative-data-stack/

7. Designing a Declarative Data Stack. The architectural decisions behind building one: config vs code, template generation vs parametric, existing orchestrators vs custom engines. https://www.rilldata.com/blog/designing-a-declarative-data-stack-from-theory-to-practice

8. Multi-Cloud Cost Analytics. A declarative stack in practice: AWS + GCP + Stripe unified into a single FinOps dashboard using dlt, Parquet, and Rill. Composable from day one. https://www.ssp.sh/blog/finops-dlt-clickhouse-rill/

9. Dlt+ClickHouse+Rill: Taking it to Production. Same stack, cloud-ready. Switching from local DuckDB to ClickHouse. https://www.rilldata.com/blog/dlt-clickhouse-rill-multi-cloud-cost-analytics-cloud-ready

What's your take? Is BI dying, or is it finally becoming what it always promised to be?
items.text_zh:
我花了20多年追踪商业智能的未来，以下是发现。2026年的BI已面目全非——从仪表盘到声明式堆栈再到智能体工程，一切都在改变。但核心本质从未动摇。

若想打通BI与数据工程，构建既能与智能体协作又不背离BI初衷的堆栈，以下9个概念值得学习：

1. **AI揭示BI为何依然重要**。提示：AI智能体对仪表盘视而不见，它们需要BI原语：指标、语义、治理。智能体依赖这些。https://www.rilldata.com/blog/ai-reveals-why-bi-still-matters-hint-its-not-dashboards

2. **自助式BI是否终因AI到来？** 经过一年MCP尝试和更长时间的语义感知逻辑层探索，AI兑现了承诺——智能体无需SQL就能自主理解业务上下文。https://www.ssp.sh/blog/self-service-bi-ai/

3. **构建智能体友好、本地优先的分析堆栈**。智能体优先BI的真实形态：本地DuckDB + MotherDuck + Rill YAML指标，LLM可解析、推理并安全修改。https://www.rilldata.com/blog/building-an-agent-friendly-local-first-analytics-stack-with-motherduck-and-rill

4. **BI即代码与GenBI新时代**。当仪表盘以YAML和SQL而非专有UI存在时，LLM能读取、生成并维护它们，实现更快的生产迭代。https://www.rilldata.com/blog/bi-as-code-and-the-new-era-of-genbi

5. **数据透视表为何永不消亡**。自1989年起它就是数据探索的通用语言。理解其本质，就能洞悉人类（及AI）与数据交互的核心。https://www.rilldata.com/blog/why-pivot-tables-never-die

6. **声明式数据堆栈的崛起**。从命令式配置到Kubernetes风格YAML的转变——这是所有上层建筑的基础。https://www.ssp.sh/blog/rise-of-declarative-data-stack/

7. **设计声明式数据堆栈**。构建过程中的架构决策：配置与代码、模板生成与参数化、现有编排器与自定义引擎。https://www.rilldata.com/blog/designing-a-declarative-data-stack-from-theory-to-practice

8. **多云成本分析**。声明式堆栈实践：通过dlt、Parquet和Rill将AWS+GCP+Stripe统一为单一FinOps仪表盘，从第一天起即可组合。https://www.ssp.sh/blog/finops-dlt-clickhouse-rill/

9. **Dlt+ClickHouse+Rill：投入生产**。相同堆栈，云端就绪——从本地DuckDB迁移至ClickHouse。https://www.rilldata.com/blog/dlt-clickhouse-rill-multi-cloud-cost-analytics-cloud-ready

你的看法是什么？BI正在消亡，还是终于成为它一直承诺的样子？

Six stages, one loop, and every prompt in the piece is yours to copy.

items.text:
we started a company!! 

so, we’re tackling continual learning: what’s the learning algorithm to take arbitrary data — documents, conversations, the models’ own experience — and make better models? how do we scale compute in the same way we’ve already seen with pre-training and inference time, but scaling on the same data we see as humans, day after day with no labels, no rewards?

A lot of the ingredients are out there already (rl, distillation, long-context, sparse / param-efficient architectures, etc.). our team is at the frontier of these topics, and we’re singularly focused on this. we want to understand this problem better than anyone else in the world.

nobody’s solved this problem yet, but even today it’s extremely greenfield opportunity to co-develop research & useful products. in our space, how people interact with the models defines what the data distribution is - and working on this problem end-to-end, from core science to end user, gives us incredible freedom to define the problem and imagine new kinds of experiences.

i expect we’ll use models that continually learn much differently than we’re using them today. it’ll feel different when the models _just know_, and build on our thinking and direction in ways we can’t even imagine. we don’t even know the queries we’re not asking, the things we would do but aren’t able to today.

i’m so excited to share what we’re doing with the world in the coming months!! 
and the team is extremely cracked :) tackling this grand challenge and working alongside @jxmnop @EyubogluSabri @dan_biderman @MayeeChen @__howardchen @shizhehe and many others has made every day so fun. come work with us!

所以，我们正在攻克持续学习这一难题：什么样的学习算法能够处理任意数据——文档、对话、模型自身的经验——并打造出更优秀的模型？我们如何像在预训练和推理阶段已经看到的那样扩展计算能力，但却是基于人类日复一日所见的相同数据，没有标签，没有奖励？

许多要素已经存在（强化学习、蒸馏、长上下文、稀疏/参数高效架构等）。我们的团队处于这些领域的前沿，并且我们专注于这一目标。我们想比世界上任何人都更深入地理解这个问题。

目前还没有人解决这个问题，但即便在今天，共同开发研究和实用产品也是一个极具潜力的蓝海领域。在我们这个领域，人们与模型互动的方式决定了数据分布——而从头到尾解决这个问题，从核心科学到最终用户，赋予我们极大的自由来定义问题并构想全新的体验。

我预计，我们使用持续学习模型的方式将与今天大不相同。当模型“自然而然就懂”，并以我们无法想象的方式构建我们的思考和方向时，感觉会完全不同。我们甚至不知道那些我们没在问的问题，那些我们想做但今天却做不到的事情。

我非常兴奋，能在未来几个月与全世界分享我们正在做的事情！！
而且团队极其强悍 :) 攻克这一宏大挑战，并与 @jxmnop @EyubogluSabri @dan_biderman @MayeeChen @__howardchen @shizhehe 以及许多其他人并肩作战，让每一天都充满乐趣。来和我们一起工作吧！

Natural language is great for one-off tasks, but suboptimal for defining system behavior.

Prompt debt creeps in with each small fix and additional instruction, until your prompt is brittle, you're afraid to touch it for fear of regression, and you're locked into one model.

A builder just declared "loops are dead," and the fight that followed talked past itself.

Three different things get called a loop. Only one is:

Routine: fixed steps, every time.
Workflow: branches on what it finds.
Loop: repeats and checks its own work until a condition holds.

The first two aren't loops. "Loops are dead" really means "routines on a timer are dead." Fair. The third kind is the one worth building.

Full guide (not only) for PMs ↓
items.text_zh:
一位构建者刚刚宣称“循环已死”，随之而来的争论却各说各话。

有三种不同的东西被称为循环，但只有一种名副其实：

- **例行程序**：固定步骤，每次重复。
- **工作流**：根据发现的情况分支。
- **循环**：重复执行并检查自身工作，直到满足某个条件。

前两种不是循环。“循环已死”实际上意味着“定时触发的例行程序已死”。这说得通。第三种才是值得构建的。

items.text:
推荐这篇文章，Anthropic 系统性地定义了"上下文工程"这个新概念。它回答了比"怎么写更好的 prompt"更根本的问题：在 LLM 注意力预算有限的前提下，什么样的上下文配置最容易触发你想要的行为。如果你在设计和维护 Agent 系统，这篇里的 compaction、渐进式检索、工具设计原则是基本功。

上下文工程：比 Prompt 工程更重要的 Agent 设计能力

Prompt 工程关注怎么写好指令。上下文工程回答一个更广的问题：在 LLM 的有限注意力预算下，什么配置的 token 最有可能产生期望的行为。

核心洞察：LLM 跟人类一样，有一个注意力预算。每个新 token 消耗一部分预算。上下文必须被视为有限资源，具有递减的边际回报。这不是软约束——是 transformer 架构的 n² 注意力关系导致的硬约束。

各层的最佳实践

系统提示应该极其清晰，用简单直接的语言，达到正确的高度——在"硬编码脆弱的 if-else 逻辑"和"过于模糊的指导"之间。curate 最小但足够的信息集，然后根据失败模式迭代添加。

工具设计上，Agent 应该定义清晰、自包含、对错误鲁棒。最常犯的错误是工具太多——如果人类工程师没法确定某个场景该用哪个工具，AI Agent 也做不到。

示例仍然是最好的实践，但不要塞一堆边缘情况。选一组多样化、规范化的例子。对 LLM 来说，示例是千言万语的图片。

长期任务的三个技巧

压缩。把接近窗口限制的对话总结成高保真摘要，开启新窗口。关键在保留什么 vs 丢弃什么。先最大化召回率、再提高精确度。

结构化笔记。Agent 定期把笔记写入上下文之外的持久存储。Claude 玩宝可梦演示了这个模式：在成千上万步游戏操作中，Agent 精确追踪进度，不用把所有信息都存在上下文里。

子 Agent 架构。一个主 Agent 协调 plan，多个专门子 Agent 各自在干净的上下文中处理深度任务。每个子 Agent 可能用上万 token，但只返回 1000-2000 token 的精炼摘要。

原文：Anthropic Engineering, "Effective context engineering for AI agents", 2025-09-29
https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents

No stop condition, so loops run forever and bill you in your sleep.

Most builders are missing at least two of the three.

items.text:
Europe cannot rent its way to AI sovereignty.

TLDR, here's my take I shared with frontier AI lab leadership this week. When Washington can disable a model overnight, the question is not whether AI is safe but who controls it:

A week ago the United States government ordered Anthropic, the world's most valuable AI startup, to shut off its most capable model, Fable, for every foreign national on earth - whether they worked for Anthropic or not. This was not an export ban on a weapon sold to an adversary. It was an instruction to disable a commercial product, four days after its release, after officials acted on a claim - which Anthropic disputed as narrow and unproven - that its safeguards could be jailbroken to expose cyber-offense capabilities.

I have spent my career around this technology, first as a graduate student and for the past decade as an investor @airstreet. In that time I have watched AI move from recommending movies to driving cars, speaking with a human voice, and editing the genome. I have also watched the debate about its risks settle on only half the question.

That debate is mostly about capability: how powerful these systems are becoming, and whether one might escape human control. Those are real questions. But they are not the only ones, and the Anthropic episode exposed the half we have neglected: access and control. The most advanced AI is built by a handful of American companies, on American soil, under American law, and what the rest of us are allowed to do with it can change on a Friday afternoon. The risk that matters today is not only that AI goes rogue, but that we do not control access to it at all.

Consider what "renting intelligence" now means in practice. A European hospital triaging scans, a bank screening fraud, a defense ministry planning for a conflict: increasingly each runs on an American AI system that's governed by its export regime. A single directive in Washington cascades, instantly, through every institution wired to that model. We have built core economic and public infrastructure on a supply that a foreign government can shut off. And while there are open-source alternatives, they're either Chinese or not at the frontier, and building European infrastructure on Chinese open weights trades one dependency for a thornier one.

And these systems are starting to improve themselves. As they do, AI stops being one industry among many and becomes the input to all the others - writing the code, running the research, designing the products, and, increasingly, generating the growth itself. Once intelligence is the engine of an economy, a country without a frontier model of its own does not lose a sector; it loses control of the inputs to everything else, and the independence that depends on them. Worse, the gap compounds: capability that improves itself gets harder to chase with every month it runs ahead. This is not a race Europe can plan to enter in a decade. The window to be a builder rather than a buyer is measured in the time it takes to stand up a cluster, not a career.

This should sting, because Europeans invented much of modern AI. DeepMind was founded in London and sold to Google in 2014, and a great deal of the talent that followed now lives in California. Today Europe faces a company worth almost $1 trillion and American tech giants spending an estimated $450 billion a year on AI infrastructure. Its answer has been the EU AI Act and a capital commitment that is a rounding error by comparison. A single American site, xAI's Colossus in Memphis, runs more than half a million GPUs. Europe has nothing remotely at that scale. The instinct to govern this technology is right, but we're off on the ambition by orders of magnitude.

It is fair to object that regulation is itself a form of power. But a rulebook is not a substitute for the thing it governs. You cannot regulate, or be cut off from, an industry you do not have.

Europe's instinct, when it is cut off, is not to build but to ask. We saw it within the week. The G7 convened in Evian and floated a "trusted partners" scheme to win back the access it had just lost, while Emmanuel Macron feted Donald Trump beneath the gilt of Versailles, the palace where France once helped midwife American independence. Two and a half centuries on, the dependency has reversed, and the posture is courtship.

None of this means Europe can match the American frontier dollar for dollar. With today's capital, it cannot, and pretending otherwise only wastes the little it has. But the goal is not parity, it is leverage. A country does not need the best model in the world to be sovereign; it needs a credible one of its own, on its own soil, good enough that being cut off is survivable rather than catastrophic. That is the difference between negotiating your access from dependence and negotiating it with an alternative in hand. The point is not to win the race. It is to make sure no one else can end it for you.

Sovereignty of that kind is something you build, and Europe has done it before. The Financial Conduct Authority's regulatory sandbox, launched in 2016, let startups test products with real customers under supervision instead of waiting years for authorization. The pro-innovation culture it signaled helped make London the fintech capital of Europe, home to Revolut, Wise, and Monzo. Government should be AI's most demanding early customer rather than writing rules for systems it has only ever imported.

Industry has to stop behaving like a tenant. Too many European companies rent the entire stack from American providers and build a thin product on top. That earns a margin and owns nothing: when the lab that supplies you decides to compete with you, or its government decides to cut you off, you have no ground to stand on. Where it counts, build and hold your own models and compute.

And our universities, which should be the source of all this, still work against it. I have argued here before that Europe's spinout system is broken, and it remains so. Too many institutions treat the companies their research creates as something to extract value from, rather than as the vehicle through which a discovery reaches the world. The best research should leave the building as a company, in addition to a paper.

We keep framing AI safety and AI ambition as a tradeoff, as though a country must choose between governing this technology and building it. It is not a choice. The safest position is not the most heavily regulated one. It is the one where the model runs on your terms, in your jurisdiction, and no one on the far side of an ocean can reach over and turn it off. Right now that finger is not ours. Until it is, every other conversation about AI risk is one we are having with someone else's permission.

---
END
items.text_zh:
欧洲无法靠租赁实现AI主权。

长话短说，这是我本周与前沿AI实验室领导层分享的观点。当华盛顿能在一天之内让一个模型下线时，问题不在于AI是否安全，而在于谁控制它：

一周前，美国政府命令全球最有价值的AI初创公司Anthropic，将其最强大的模型Fable对地球上所有外国公民关闭——无论他们是否为Anthropic工作。这不是针对向对手出售武器的出口禁令。这是一道指令，要求在其发布四天后禁用一款商业产品，起因是官员们根据一项声称（Anthropic认为该声称狭隘且未经证实）采取行动，称其安全防护措施可能被越狱，从而暴露网络攻击能力。

我职业生涯的大部分时间都围绕这项技术，最初是研究生，过去十年则是@airstreet的投资人。在此期间，我目睹了AI从推荐电影发展到驾驶汽车、以人类声音说话以及编辑基因组。我也看到关于其风险的讨论只停留在问题的一半。

这场讨论主要围绕能力：这些系统变得多么强大，以及是否可能脱离人类控制。这些都是真实的问题。但它们并非唯一的问题，而Anthropic事件暴露了我们忽视的另一半：访问和控制。最先进的AI由少数美国公司在美国本土、根据美国法律构建，而我们其他人被允许用它做什么，可以在一个周五下午就改变。今天真正重要的风险不仅是AI失控，而是我们根本无法控制对它的访问。

想想"租用智能"在实践中意味着什么。一家欧洲医院处理扫描图像、一家银行筛查欺诈、一个国防部规划冲突：它们越来越多地运行在受美国出口制度管辖的美国AI系统上。华盛顿的一项指令会瞬间级联，影响到每一个与该模型相连的机构。我们已经将核心经济和公共基础设施建立在一个外国政府可以随时切断的供应之上。虽然有开源替代方案，但它们要么来自中国，要么不在前沿水平，而在中国开源权重上构建欧洲基础设施，是用一种更棘手的依赖取代另一种。

而且这些系统正在开始自我改进。随着这种情况发生，AI不再只是众多行业中的一个，而是成为所有其他行业的输入——编写代码、进行研究、设计产品，并日益成为增长本身的驱动力。一旦智能成为经济的引擎，一个没有自己前沿模型的国家失去的不是一个行业，而是对一切其他输入的控制权，以及依赖这些输入的独立性。更糟的是，差距会自我强化：自我改进的能力每领先一个月，就越难追赶。这不是欧洲可以计划在十年后进入的竞赛。成为建设者而非购买者的窗口，是以搭建一个集群所需的时间来衡量的，而不是以职业生涯来衡量。

这应该让人感到刺痛，因为欧洲人发明了现代AI的很大一部分。DeepMind在伦敦创立，2014年卖给了谷歌，此后大量人才现在生活在加州。今天，欧洲面对一家价值近1万亿美元的公司，以及美国科技巨头每年估计在AI基础设施上花费4500亿美元。它的回应是欧盟AI法案和一个相比之下微不足道的资本承诺。仅美国的一个站点——xAI在孟菲斯的Colossus——就运行着超过50万个GPU。欧洲没有任何接近这个规模的东西。管理这项技术的本能是对的，但我们的雄心差了数个数量级。

反对意见认为监管本身就是一种权力形式，这很合理。但一本规则手册不能替代它所管理的东西。你不能监管一个你根本不拥有的行业，也不能被切断与它的联系。

欧洲在被切断联系时的本能不是去建设，而是去请求。我们在那一周内就看到了。七国集团在埃维昂开会，提出了一个"可信伙伴"计划，以赢回刚刚失去的访问权，而埃马纽埃尔·马克龙则在凡尔赛宫的金碧辉煌下款待唐纳德·特朗普——这座宫殿曾是法国帮助催生美国独立的地方。两个半世纪后，依赖关系已经逆转，姿态变成了求爱。

这并不意味着欧洲可以在每一美元上都与美国前沿匹敌。以今天的资本，它做不到，假装相反只会浪费它仅有的一点资源。但目标不是对等，而是杠杆。一个国家不需要拥有世界上最好的模型才能实现主权；它需要在自己的土地上拥有一个可信的、自己的模型，好到被切断联系是可控的而非灾难性的。这就是从依赖地位谈判你的访问权，与手握替代方案进行谈判之间的区别。关键不在于赢得比赛。而在于确保没有其他人能为你结束比赛。

这种主权是你自己建设出来的，欧洲以前做到过。英国金融行为监管局于2016年推出的监管沙盒，允许初创公司在监管下与真实客户测试产品，而不是等待数年的授权。它所传达的支持创新的文化，帮助伦敦成为欧洲的金融科技之都，孕育了Revolut、Wise和Monzo。政府应该成为AI最苛刻的早期客户，而不是为它只曾进口的系统制定规则。

行业必须停止表现得像个租户。太多的欧洲公司从美国提供商那里租用整个技术栈，然后在上面构建一个薄薄的产品层。这赚取了一点利润，却一无所有：当供应你的实验室决定与你竞争，或者其政府决定切断你的联系时，你将没有立足之地。在关键之处，要构建并持有你自己的模型和算力。

而我们的大学，本应是这一切的源头，却仍在与之背道而驰。我之前在这里论证过，欧洲的衍生公司体系已经崩溃，现在依然如此。太多机构将其研究创造的公司视为可以榨取价值的东西，而不是作为发现走向世界的载体。最好的研究应该以公司的形式离开大楼，而不仅仅是论文。

我们一直将AI安全与AI雄心视为一种权衡，好像一个国家必须在管理这项技术和建设它之间做出选择。这不是一个选择。最安全的立场不是监管最严格的立场。而是模型在你的条款下、在你的管辖区内运行，并且大洋彼岸没有人能伸手把它关掉。现在，那个开关不在我们手中。直到它在我们手中之前，关于AI风险的每一次其他对话，都是我们在得到别人许可的情况下进行的。

本次改版的核心是保证“流”的流动. 这个听上去很飘渺, 但是任何系统其实底层都是流, 一个完整的流动. 我希望用户在使用这个产品的时候, 一不会因为附加功能从而破坏心流, 二作为写作工具, 所有的功能应该围绕写来做, 而不是相反. 以写为起点，也以写为终点。视写为核心周期，所有的操作应该始为写，终为写. 也就是以balance loop 为核心, 配合不同的reinforcing loop 去辅助用户怎么去写的更好

这次V2也适配了新的Guardian系统, 更有效的去提供修改建议. Guardian系统我也专门写了一个paper投稿了EMNLP

新时代的ui, 是否还是以三栏为主或是大面积的数据展示为主, 我的答案是“否”. 在AI能够快速迭代需求的情况下, 剥开行为和用户心理的核心为导向的交互才是重点. 反思v1的版本, 当时做了大量借鉴IDE和已有产品的思路, 但是在实际自己使用的时候还是大量摩擦. 所以我完全推翻了之前的交互体验. 提出了这个新UI

EVERYONE IS STILL OPTIMIZING PROMPTS. THE BUILDERS SHIPPING AGENTS THAT ACTUALLY WORK MOVED ON TO SOMETHING ELSE, AND ALMOST NOBODY IS TALKING ABOUT IT

It's called context engineering

Your agent is great for the first 10 steps

Then it gets sloppy

Wrong tool calls. Forgotten instructions. Weak outputs

It's almost never the model

It's what the model is seeing

Every step dumps more into the context window

Tool results. Fetched web pages. Conversation history

It piles up, and the model's reasoning degrades long before the token limit

A 200K-token window can start slipping at 50K

This is called context rot. It's real and it's measured

This is not about buying a bigger context window

It's about controlling what the model sees at every step

LangChain boils the whole skill into four moves

Write. Persist info outside the window so the agent never loses it

Select. Load only what this step needs, not all 40 tools at once

Compress. Summarize and trim as the agent works

Isolate. Separate jobs get separate context windows. No contamination

Think about what this means

Same models. Same APIs. Same prompts

One builder's agent dies at step 20. The other's runs for hours

The only difference is who controls the context

This is the highest-leverage skill in AI agents right now, and almost nobody is teaching it

Bookmark this before your next agent build

## 所有人仍在优化提示词。真正交付可用智能体的开发者早已转向另一件事，却几乎无人提及

它叫做**上下文工程**

你的智能体在前10步表现完美

随后开始变得混乱

错误的工具调用。遗忘的指令。低质量的输出

问题几乎从来不在模型本身

每一步都会向上下文窗口倾倒更多信息

工具返回结果。抓取的网页。对话历史

这些信息不断堆积，模型在达到token限制之前很久就开始出现推理退化

一个20万token的窗口可能在5万token时就开始失效

这被称为**上下文腐烂**。它是真实存在的，并且已被量化

这不是关于购买更大的上下文窗口

而是关于控制模型在每一步所看到的内容

LangChain将整个技能归结为四个动作

**写入**。将信息持久化存储在窗口之外，这样智能体永远不会丢失它

**压缩**。在智能体工作过程中进行总结和精简

**隔离**。不同的任务使用独立的上下文窗口。没有污染

思考这意味着什么

相同的模型。相同的API。相同的提示词

一个开发者的智能体在第20步崩溃。另一个的智能体能持续运行数小时

唯一的区别在于谁控制了上下文

items.text:
Andrej Karpathy: "90% of Claude's mistakes come from missing context, not a weak model."

41% mistake rate without a CLAUDE.md. 11% with the 4-rule baseline. 3% with the 12-rule version below

here are the 12 rules senior engineers settled on:

1. think before coding: state assumptions, don't guess. the model can't read your mind, stop hoping it will

2. simplicity first: minimum code, no speculative abstractions. the moment you let Claude add "for future flexibility," you've added 200 lines you'll delete next quarter

3. surgical changes: touch only what you must. don't let it improve adjacent code, that's how PRs blow up

4. goal-driven execution: define success criteria upfront, loop until verified. without them Claude either loops forever or stops too early

5. use the model only for judgment calls: classification, drafting, summarization, extraction. NOT routing, retries, status-code handling, deterministic transforms. if code can answer, code answers

6. token budgets are not advisory: per-task 4000, per-session 30000. by message 40 of a long debug, Claude is re-suggesting fixes you rejected at message 5

7. surface conflicts, don't average them: two patterns in the codebase? pick one. Claude blending them is how errors get swallowed twice

8. read before you write: read exports, callers, shared utilities. Claude will happily add a duplicate function next to an identical one it never read

9. tests verify intent, not just behavior: a test that can't fail when business logic changes is wrong. all 12 of Claude's tests can pass while the function returns a constant

10. checkpoint every significant step: Claude finished steps 5 and 6 on top of a broken state from step 4. nobody noticed for an hour

11. match the codebase conventions: class components? don't fork to hooks silently. testing patterns assumed componentDidMount, hooks broke them without surfacing

12. fail loud: "completed successfully" with 14% of records silently skipped is the worst class of bug. surface uncertainty, don't hide it

what actually compounds instead of the next framework:

- the CLAUDE.md file as institutional memory across sessions
- eval-driven changes, not vibe-driven
- checkpoints over speed
- explicit conflicts over silent blending
- discipline over framework, every time
- one repo, one rules file, no exceptions

you don't need a better AI 

you need better context engineering  

complete playbook below ↓
items.text_zh:
Andrej Karpathy："Claude 90% 的错误源于上下文缺失，而非模型本身不够强。"

无 CLAUDE.md 时错误率 41%。使用 4 条基础规则降至 11%。采用以下 12 条规则版本后降至 3%。

以下是资深工程师最终确定的 12 条规则：

1.  先思考再编码：陈述假设，不要猜测。模型无法读懂你的心思，别指望它能。
2.  简洁至上：代码量最小化，不做推测性抽象。一旦你让 Claude 添加"为了未来灵活性"，你就多写了 200 行下个季度要删的代码。
3.  精准修改：只动必须动的地方。别让它"顺便改进"相邻代码，那是 PR 失控的根源。
4.  目标驱动执行：预先定义成功标准，循环验证直至达标。没有标准，Claude 要么无限循环，要么过早停止。
5.  仅将模型用于判断性任务：分类、起草、总结、提取。不要用于路由、重试、状态码处理、确定性转换。如果代码能回答，就让代码回答。
6.  Token 预算不是建议：每任务 4000，每会话 30000。在长调试会话的第 40 条消息时，Claude 会重新建议你在第 5 条消息时已拒绝的修复方案。
7.  暴露冲突，不要折中：代码库中有两种模式？选一种。Claude 将它们混合，会导致错误被双重掩盖。
8.  先读后写：先读取导出、调用者、共享工具。Claude 会愉快地在旁边添加一个重复函数，而它从未读过那个已存在的相同函数。
9.  测试验证意图，而不仅仅是行为：一个在业务逻辑变化时仍能通过的测试是错误的。Claude 的 12 个测试可能全部通过，而函数返回的却是一个常量。
10. 每个重要步骤后设置检查点：Claude 在第 4 步的损坏状态基础上完成了第 5 和第 6 步。一小时后才有人发现。
11. 匹配代码库约定：使用类组件？不要默默切换到 Hooks。测试模式假设了 componentDidMount，Hooks 破坏了它们却没有暴露问题。
12. 失败要响亮："成功完成"但 14% 的记录被静默跳过，这是最糟糕的 bug 类型。暴露不确定性，不要隐藏它。

真正起作用的，不是下一个框架：

-   CLAUDE.md 文件作为跨会话的机构记忆
-   评估驱动的变更，而非感觉驱动
-   检查点优于速度
-   显式冲突优于静默混合
-   纪律优于框架，始终如此
-   一个仓库，一个规则文件，没有例外

你不需要更好的 AI

你需要更好的上下文工程

完整行动手册 ↓

items.text:
loop engineering only holds up if the loop can remember. what that actually means:

without memory:
-> the constraint on a long-running loop was never intelligence or prompting, it's memory. the loop outran what it could hold
-> the real damage isn't forgetting. the loop re-ingests its own output, so an early mistake becomes ground truth for every pass after. it launders its own mistakes into facts
-> 900 passes later it's exactly where pass 1 was, and no prompt fixes that

with memory:
-> recall isn't the test. the question a loop actually asks is, given attempts 1 through 46, what do you do on 47
-> a flat MEMORY.md isn't a memory system. it rots, bloats context, and matches on keywords. you want recall by meaning, with facts that update in place
-> that's what turns the circle into a spiral. the loop gives an agent persistence across time, memory gives it persistence across forgetting

the memory layer is the whole difference
items.text_zh:
循环工程只有在循环能够“记住”时才成立。这实际意味着：

**没有记忆时：**
→ 长时循环的瓶颈从来不是智能或提示词，而是记忆——循环会超出其承载能力
→ 真正的损害并非遗忘。循环会重新摄入自身输出，早期的一个错误会成为后续每一轮迭代的“基准事实”。它把自己的错误洗白成事实
→ 900轮迭代后，它仍停留在第1轮的位置，没有任何提示词能修复这个问题

**拥有记忆时：**
→ 考验不在于“回忆”。循环真正问的问题是：给定第1到第46次尝试，第47次该怎么做？
→ 一个扁平的 MEMORY.md 文件不是记忆系统。它会腐化、膨胀上下文，且仅靠关键词匹配。你需要的是按语义召回，且事实能原地更新
→ 这正是把“圆圈”变成“螺旋”的关键。循环赋予智能体跨越时间的持久性，记忆则赋予它跨越遗忘的持久性

记忆层就是全部的区别所在。

items.text_zh:
# 推理工程深度解析

推理工程（Inference Engineering）是人工智能领域中一个快速发展的分支，专注于优化和部署训练好的机器学习模型，使其能够在生产环境中高效运行。与模型训练不同，推理工程关注的是模型在部署后的性能、延迟、吞吐量和资源利用率。

## 核心概念

### 1. 推理优化技术

推理工程涉及多种优化技术，包括：

- **模型量化**：将模型权重从FP32降低到INT8或FP16，显著减少内存占用和计算需求
- **知识蒸馏**：将大型教师模型的知识迁移到更小的学生模型
- **剪枝**：移除对模型输出影响较小的神经元或连接
- **算子融合**：将多个连续操作合并为单一操作，减少内存访问开销

### 2. 推理引擎与框架

主流推理引擎包括：

- **TensorRT**：NVIDIA的高性能推理优化器，支持层融合、精度校准和内核自动调优
- **ONNX Runtime**：跨平台推理引擎，支持多种硬件加速器
- **OpenVINO**：Intel的推理优化工具套件
- **vLLM**：专为大语言模型设计的高吞吐量推理引擎
- **llama.cpp**：轻量级LLM推理实现，支持CPU推理

### 3. 服务架构

现代推理系统通常采用以下架构模式：

- **批处理推理**：将多个请求合并为批次处理，提高GPU利用率
- **连续批处理**：动态管理请求队列，实现实时流式推理
- **模型并行**：将大型模型分布到多个设备上
- **流水线并行**：将模型层分布到不同设备，实现流水线处理

## 关键挑战

### 延迟与吞吐量的平衡

推理工程需要在响应时间和处理能力之间找到最佳平衡点。对于实时应用（如聊天机器人），低延迟至关重要；而对于离线批处理任务，高吞吐量更为重要。

### 内存管理

大型语言模型（LLM）通常需要数十GB的显存。有效的内存管理策略包括：

- **KV缓存优化**：使用PagedAttention等技术管理注意力机制的键值缓存
- **内存卸载**：将不活跃的层卸载到CPU内存
- **前缀缓存**：缓存共享提示词的计算结果

### 硬件适配

不同硬件平台需要不同的优化策略：

- GPU：利用Tensor Core、CUDA图优化
- CPU：使用AVX指令集、MKL加速
- 专用芯片：适配TPU、NPU等定制加速器

## 实践案例

### 大语言模型推理

以LLM推理为例，现代推理系统通常采用以下技术栈：

1. **模型加载**：使用量化技术（如GPTQ、AWQ）压缩模型
2. **推理引擎**：选择vLLM或TensorRT-LLM
3. **服务框架**：通过FastAPI或Triton Inference Server暴露API
4. **监控与调优**：使用Prometheus和Grafana监控性能指标

### 性能基准测试

评估推理系统时，常用指标包括：

- **首Token延迟**：从请求到生成第一个token的时间
- **Token生成速率**：每秒生成的token数量
- **并发处理能力**：同时处理的请求数量
- **内存占用**：推理过程中的峰值内存使用

## 未来趋势

推理工程正在向以下方向发展：

- **自适应推理**：根据输入复杂度动态调整计算资源
- **稀疏推理**：利用模型稀疏性减少计算量
- **边缘推理**：将推理能力部署到移动设备和IoT设备
- **多模态推理**：支持文本、图像、音频等多种输入类型

## 总结

推理工程是连接AI研究与实际应用的关键桥梁。随着模型规模不断增长和应用场景日益复杂，高效的推理技术将成为AI落地的核心竞争力。掌握推理工程不仅需要理解底层硬件特性，还需要熟悉各种优化算法和系统设计模式。

最近大家都在聊 agent 的「loop」，但很少人讲清它到底是什么。Warp CEO Zach Lloyd 给了一个能落地的版本：让 Skill 从反馈里自我进化的双层循环，以 GitHub issue 三分类为例。

内循环：每来一个新 issue，GitHub Action 触发云 agent 跑 triage Skill，自动分到 ready-to-implement / needs-info / duplicate 三档，打标签并发一条带隐藏标记 oz-triage v:N 的评论，求 👍/👎。

外循环：每天一个定时 agent 拉取近 14 天所有被分类的 issue，收集三类信号，评论赞踩、人工纠正回复，还有「人把标签从 ready 改成 needs-info」这种标签漂移（最强 ground truth）。然后把信号提炼成可泛化规则，比如别盯着单个 issue 改，而是写成「崩溃报告缺 OS 版本号一律归 needs-info」，再塞进 Skill 的 Learned guidelines 段、版本号 +1，开 PR 让人 review 合并，永不自动改 main。

要点就一句：Skill 就是文件，改进 = 对文件做 diff；反馈天然藏在 issue 标签和评论里，零额外标注成本。同样适用于 code review、bug 修复、事件响应；目标明确时可用自动 grader 替代人工。Warp 已用它管理自家开源仓库并开源了框架（oz-for-oss）。
最好的coding workflow skills，没有之一。
